zh: 只要没被锁住，来什么接什么。这套玩法的基准。
en: Accept whatever comes whenever you are not locked. The benchmark for this game.

zh: 没有优化目标：它衡量的是"完全不挑"能拿到多少。
en: There is no optimization objective: it measures how much you get by "not being picky at all".

zh: 不是最优。报价的均值是 1，每接一单占用 $1+L$ 回合，所以长期平均收益恰好是 $\dfrac{1}{1+L}$（$L=15$ 时是 $0.0625$）。长期平均意义下，它最优当且仅当最优门槛 $c^*$ 不高于报价的下界 $x_{\min}$，也就是 $L\,(1-x_{\min})\le x_{\min}$。报价可以任意接近 0（指数、均匀、对数正态）时，只有 $L=0$ 才行；帕累托分布的报价有正的下界 $(\alpha-1)/\alpha$，$L\le\alpha-1$ 时见单就接就是最优的门槛规则（比如 $\alpha=2.5$、$L=1$）。报价可以为负时，它还会接下亏本的单。
en: Not optimal. The mean offer is 1 and each accepted offer takes up $1+L$ rounds, so the long-run average payoff is exactly $\dfrac{1}{1+L}$ ($0.0625$ when $L=15$). In the long-run average sense, it is optimal if and only if the optimal threshold $c^*$ is no higher than the lower bound $x_{\min}$ of the offers, that is, $L\,(1-x_{\min})\le x_{\min}$. When offers can be arbitrarily close to 0 (exponential, uniform, lognormal), this holds only for $L=0$; Pareto offers have a positive lower bound $(\alpha-1)/\alpha$, and when $L\le\alpha-1$ taking every offer is the optimal threshold rule (for example $\alpha=2.5$, $L=1$). When offers can be negative, it also accepts offers that lose money.

zh: 锁得越久、报价越分散，它丢掉的越多：好单来的时候它多半正被一张小单锁着。报价可以为负时它还会把亏本的单也接下来。
en: The longer the lock and the more dispersed the offers, the more it gives up: when a good offer arrives, it is most likely locked by a small one. When offers can be negative, it accepts the money-losing ones as well.

zh: 把"锁几回合"调成 0，它应该追平所有规则；调大以后，它与固定门槛的差距越拉越大。
en: Set "Rounds locked after accepting an offer" to 0 and it should pull even with all the other rules; as you raise it, the gap between it and the fixed threshold keeps widening.

zh: 报价不低于 c 才接。
en: Accept an offer only if it is at least c.

zh: 门槛 c
en: Threshold c

zh: 指数分布、锁 15 回合时的最优值约为 2.01
en: With exponential offers and a 15-round lock, the optimal value is about 2.01

zh: 报价 $X_1,X_2,\dots$ 独立同分布，分布已知，$\mathbb{E}|X|<\infty$。接一单之后锁 $L$ 回合。
en: The offers $X_1,X_2,\dots$ are i.i.d. with a known distribution and $\mathbb{E}|X|<\infty$. After you accept an offer you are locked for $L$ rounds.

zh: 长期平均收益 $\rho=\lim_{T\to\infty}\dfrac1T\,\mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_{t\le T}X_t\,\mathbf 1\{\text{第 }t\text{ 回合接单}\}\Big]$。
en: The long-run average payoff $\rho=\lim_{T\to\infty}\dfrac1T\,\mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_{t\le T}X_t\,\mathbf 1\{\text{the offer in round }t\text{ is accepted}\}\Big]$.

zh:
**定理。** 门槛规则"$X\ge c$ 就接"的长期平均收益是
$$\rho(c)=\frac{\mathbb{E}[X;\,X\ge c]}{1+L\,\mathbb{P}(X\ge c)}.$$
在所有只依赖历史的规则里，$\rho$ 的最大值由门槛 $c^*$ 取到；$L\ge1$ 时 $c^*$ 是方程 $c=L\,\mathbb{E}(X-c)^+$ 的唯一解，并且 $\rho^*=c^*/L$。

**证明思路。** 用更新报酬定理：一个周期 = 等到第一个不低于 $c$ 的报价（几何分布，平均 $1/q$ 回合，$q=\mathbb{P}(X\ge c)$），再加 $L$ 回合的锁定；周期平均长 $1/q+L$，周期收益的期望是 $\mathbb{E}[X\mid X\ge c]$，相除即得 $\rho(c)$。最优性来自平均报酬的动态规划：设最优平均收益为 $\rho^*$。接单占掉 $1+L$ 回合，放过占掉 1 回合，所以应当接下 $x$ 当且仅当 $x-(1+L)\rho^*\ge-\rho^*$，即 $x\ge L\rho^*$。于是最优规则是门槛 $c^*=L\rho^*=L\rho(c^*)$，整理后就是 $c^*=L\,\mathbb{E}(X-c^*)^+$。这个方程左边递增、右边递减，解唯一。

报价服从 $\mathrm{Exp}(1)$ 时 $\mathbb{E}(X-c)^+=e^{-c}$，方程成了 $c\,e^{c}=L$，即 $c^*=W(L)$（Lambert $W$ 函数）。$L=15$ 时 $c^*\approx2.010$，$\rho^*\approx0.134$，是见单就接（$1/16=0.0625$）的两倍多。对数正态时 $\mathbb{E}(X-c)^+$ 就是 Black–Scholes 的看涨期权公式。
en:
**Theorem.** The threshold rule "accept if $X\ge c$" has long-run average payoff
$$\rho(c)=\frac{\mathbb{E}[X;\,X\ge c]}{1+L\,\mathbb{P}(X\ge c)}.$$
Among all rules that depend only on the history, the maximum of $\rho$ is attained by the threshold $c^*$; for $L\ge1$, $c^*$ is the unique solution of the equation $c=L\,\mathbb{E}(X-c)^+$, and $\rho^*=c^*/L$.

**Proof sketch.** Use the renewal reward theorem: one cycle = the wait for the first offer of at least $c$ (geometric, $1/q$ rounds on average, $q=\mathbb{P}(X\ge c)$) plus the $L$ locked rounds; the mean cycle length is $1/q+L$ and the expected payoff per cycle is $\mathbb{E}[X\mid X\ge c]$, and dividing one by the other gives $\rho(c)$. Optimality comes from average-reward dynamic programming: let the optimal average payoff be $\rho^*$. Accepting takes up $1+L$ rounds and passing takes up 1 round, so you should accept $x$ if and only if $x-(1+L)\rho^*\ge-\rho^*$, that is, $x\ge L\rho^*$. The optimal rule is therefore the threshold $c^*=L\rho^*=L\rho(c^*)$, which rearranges to $c^*=L\,\mathbb{E}(X-c^*)^+$. The left side of this equation is increasing and the right side is decreasing, so the solution is unique.

When offers are $\mathrm{Exp}(1)$, $\mathbb{E}(X-c)^+=e^{-c}$ and the equation becomes $c\,e^{c}=L$, that is, $c^*=W(L)$ (the Lambert $W$ function). For $L=15$, $c^*\approx2.010$ and $\rho^*\approx0.134$, more than twice the payoff of taking every offer ($1/16=0.0625$). For lognormal offers, $\mathbb{E}(X-c)^+$ is the Black–Scholes call option formula.

zh: 回合数有限时，最后几回合应该把门槛降下来（最后一回合只要不亏就该接）；再往前一点，在还剩 $L$ 回合上下的地方，门槛反而要比 $c^*$ 高，因为这时接一单就等于放弃剩下的全部回合。固定门槛为此损失 $O(L/T)$ 的量级。分布要靠估计，或者会随时间变时，$c^*$ 跟着不准。报价之间有相关性（好单扎堆出现）时，最优规则要看当前的状态，不再是一个常数门槛。
en: When the number of rounds is finite, the threshold should come down in the last few rounds (in the last round you should accept anything that does not lose money); a little earlier, with about $L$ rounds left, the threshold should instead be higher than $c^*$, because accepting an offer at that point means giving up all the remaining rounds. The fixed threshold loses an amount of order $O(L/T)$ because of this. When the distribution has to be estimated, or changes over time, $c^*$ is off accordingly. When offers are correlated (good offers arrive in clusters), the optimal rule has to look at the current state and is no longer a constant threshold.

zh: 对门槛 $c$ 做扫描：得分曲线应与图上的理论曲线 $\rho(c)$ 重合，峰值在 $c^*$。把报价分布换成帕累托或均匀分布，峰值的位置跟着变（当前的 $c^*$ 写在结果栏对照表里"固定门槛"那一行的名字上）。
en: Sweep the threshold $c$: the score curve should coincide with the theoretical curve $\rho(c)$ on the chart, with its peak at $c^*$. Switch the offer distribution to Pareto or uniform and the peak moves with it (the current $c^*$ appears in the name of the "fixed threshold" row of the comparison table in the results bar).

zh: 先从另一批对局里估出报价的分布，再倒推每一回合的门槛：越到后面越不挑。
en: First estimate the offer distribution from a separate batch of episodes, then work backward to find the threshold for each round: the later the round, the less picky.

zh: 报价独立同分布。分布本身不必事先知道：用另外一批对局里的两万个报价当作它的经验分布。回合数 $T$ 和锁定长度 $L$ 已知。
en: The offers are i.i.d. The distribution itself need not be known in advance: 20,000 offers from a separate batch of episodes serve as its empirical distribution. The number of rounds $T$ and the lock length $L$ are known.

zh: 一局（有限的 $T$ 回合）的期望总收益。
en: The expected total payoff of one episode (a finite number $T$ of rounds).

zh:
**有限期下精确最优（给定分布）。** 令 $V_t$ 为"第 $t$ 回合开始时没被锁"之后还能拿到的最优期望总收益，$V_t=0$（$t\ge T$）。Bellman 方程是
$$V_t=\mathbb{E}\max\big(X+V_{t+L+1},\ V_{t+1}\big)=V_{t+1}+\mathbb{E}\,(X-c_t)^+,\qquad c_t=V_{t+1}-V_{t+L+1}.$$
最优动作是"$X\ge c_t$ 就接"。离终局很远时 $c_t$ 趋于稳态门槛 $c^*$；最后 $L+1$ 回合里 $V_{t+L+1}=0$，门槛一路降到最后一回合的 $0$。
代码里用经验分布代替真实分布：把样本排序、做后缀和，$\mathbb{E}(X-c)^+$ 用一次二分查找算出，整张门槛表的计算量是 $O(m\log m+T\log m)$（$m$ 是样本数），存储是 $O(m+T)$。
en:
**Exactly optimal over a finite horizon (given the distribution).** Let $V_t$ be the optimal expected total payoff that can still be collected from "not locked at the start of round $t$" onward, with $V_t=0$ ($t\ge T$). The Bellman equation is
$$V_t=\mathbb{E}\max\big(X+V_{t+L+1},\ V_{t+1}\big)=V_{t+1}+\mathbb{E}\,(X-c_t)^+,\qquad c_t=V_{t+1}-V_{t+L+1}.$$
The optimal action is "accept if $X\ge c_t$". Far from the end of the episode, $c_t$ tends to the steady-state threshold $c^*$; in the last $L+1$ rounds $V_{t+L+1}=0$, and the threshold falls all the way to $0$ in the last round.
The code uses the empirical distribution in place of the true one: it sorts the sample and takes suffix sums, so that $\mathbb{E}(X-c)^+$ is computed with one binary search; the computation for the whole threshold table is $O(m\log m+T\log m)$ ($m$ is the sample size) and the memory is $O(m+T)$.

zh: 训练用的那批对局和真正要玩的不是同一个分布时，门槛跟着错。相对固定门槛的优势只有 $O(L/T)$：$T=2000$、$L=15$ 时大约是千分之一（0.1345 对 0.1344），单看各自的得分分不出来，要看同一批对局上的配对差。
en: When the batch of episodes used for training and the episodes actually played do not have the same distribution, the thresholds are wrong accordingly. The advantage over the fixed threshold is only $O(L/T)$: for $T=2000$, $L=15$ it is about one part in a thousand (0.1345 versus 0.1344), which you cannot tell from the two scores taken separately; you have to look at the paired difference on the same batch of episodes.

zh: 把一局缩短到 100 回合：终局效应占的比重变大，它对固定门槛的领先应该变得清楚。规则下方会显示倒推出的开局门槛和最后一回合的门槛。
en: Shorten the episode to 100 rounds: the end-of-episode effect carries more weight, and its lead over the fixed threshold should become clear. Below the rule, the thresholds obtained by backward induction for the start of the episode and for the last round are displayed.

zh: 不知道分布：每看到一个报价，就把门槛朝最优值挪一小步（随机逼近）。
en: The distribution is unknown: with every offer seen, move the threshold a small step toward the optimal value (stochastic approximation).

zh: 起始门槛
en: Initial threshold

zh: 步长系数 a
en: Step-size coefficient a

zh: 步长的延迟 b
en: Step-size delay b

zh: 第 n 次修正的步长是 a/(n + b)；b 大一些，开局时不会被头几个报价带着乱跳
en: The step size of the n-th update is a/(n + b); a larger b keeps the threshold from being jerked around by the first few offers at the start of the episode

zh: 报价独立同分布，但分布未知。被锁住的回合照样看得到报价。
en: The offers are i.i.d., but the distribution is unknown. Offers remain visible during the rounds when you are locked.

zh: 找到方程 $h(c)=L\,\mathbb{E}(X-c)^+-c=0$ 的根 $c^*$，也就是长期平均收益最大的门槛，同时边学边接单。
en: Find the root $c^*$ of the equation $h(c)=L\,\mathbb{E}(X-c)^+-c=0$, that is, the threshold with the highest long-run average payoff, while accepting offers as it learns.

zh:
**定理（随机逼近：Robbins–Monro 1951；几乎必然收敛见 Blum 1954）。** $h$ 严格递减，根唯一。迭代
$$c_{n+1}=c_n+a_n\big(L\,(X_n-c_n)^+-c_n\big),\qquad \textstyle\sum a_n=\infty,\ \sum a_n^2<\infty,$$
在 $\mathbb{E}X^2<\infty$ 时几乎必然收敛到 $c^*$。括号里的量是 $h(c_n)$ 的无偏估计：只用到当前这一个报价，所以每一步的计算量和存储量都是 $O(1)$，不需要记住历史。
步长取 $a_n=a/(n+b)$。$a>\dfrac{1}{2|h'(c^*)|}$ 时误差按 $n^{-1/2}$ 的速度缩小（$|h'(c^*)|=1+L\,\mathbb{P}(X\ge c^*)$）。
它只是渐近最优：学习期间门槛不准，这部分损失算在得分里。
en:
**Theorem (stochastic approximation: Robbins–Monro 1951; for almost sure convergence see Blum 1954).** $h$ is strictly decreasing and its root is unique. The iteration
$$c_{n+1}=c_n+a_n\big(L\,(X_n-c_n)^+-c_n\big),\qquad \textstyle\sum a_n=\infty,\ \sum a_n^2<\infty,$$
converges almost surely to $c^*$ when $\mathbb{E}X^2<\infty$. The quantity in parentheses is an unbiased estimate of $h(c_n)$: it uses only the current offer, so the computation and the memory per step are both $O(1)$, and there is no need to remember the history.
The step size is $a_n=a/(n+b)$. When $a>\dfrac{1}{2|h'(c^*)|}$, the error shrinks at the rate $n^{-1/2}$ ($|h'(c^*)|=1+L\,\mathbb{P}(X\ge c^*)$).
It is only asymptotically optimal: the threshold is inaccurate while it is learning, and that loss counts in the score.

zh: 厚尾的报价（帕累托、$\alpha\le2$ 时方差不存在）会让门槛被偶尔出现的巨大报价猛推一把，收敛很慢甚至不收敛。步长系数太小则学得太慢，一局结束了还没到位。分布中途改变时，递减的步长跟不上（那时该用固定的小步长）。
en: With heavy-tailed offers (Pareto, where the variance does not exist for $\alpha\le2$), an occasional huge offer gives the threshold a violent push, and convergence is very slow or does not happen at all. If the step-size coefficient is too small, it learns too slowly and has not settled by the end of the episode. When the distribution changes midway, a decreasing step size cannot keep up (a small constant step size should be used in that case).

zh: 在指数分布下它应当只比已知分布的固定门槛差一点点；换成帕累托分布，差距变大。对步长系数 $a$ 做扫描，得分是一个平缓的单峰。
en: Under the exponential distribution it should be only slightly worse than the fixed threshold computed from the known distribution; switch to the Pareto distribution and the gap widens. Sweep the step-size coefficient $a$: the score has a single, gentle peak.

zh: 不观察，不比较。这套玩法的基准。
en: No observing, no comparing. The benchmark for this game.

zh: 不是最优。候选人的次序是均匀随机的，第一个人恰好是全场最好的概率是 $1/n$；他的名次在 $1,\dots,n$ 上均匀分布，期望名次是 $(n+1)/2$。任何"事先定好选第几个"的规则都是这个成绩。
en: Not optimal. The order of the candidates is uniformly random, so the probability that the first candidate happens to be the best overall is $1/n$; that candidate's rank is uniformly distributed on $1,\dots,n$, and the expected rank is $(n+1)/2$. Any rule that "fixes in advance which arrival to pick" gets the same result.

zh: 它没有用到任何信息，所以也谈不上失效。
en: It uses no information at all, so there is nothing that can fail.

zh: 得分应为 $1/n$（目标是选中最好的）或 $\tfrac12$（目标是名次）。
en: The score should be $1/n$ (when the objective is to pick the best) or $\tfrac12$ (when the objective is rank).

zh: 前 m 个人只看不选，之后遇到第一个比之前都好的就要。
en: Look at the first m candidates without picking; after that, take the first one who is better than everyone before.

zh: 先看多少人 m
en: Candidates to look at first m

zh: n = 100 时最优是 37，约等于 n/e
en: For n = 100 the optimum is 37, approximately n/e

zh: $n$ 个候选人的优劣次序是 $n!$ 种排列里均匀随机的一种；每来一个人，只能看到他在已经见过的人里排第几（相对名次）；整局只能选一个，放过的不能回头。
en: The quality ranking of the $n$ candidates is one of the $n!$ permutations, chosen uniformly at random; as each candidate arrives, you see only that candidate's rank among those seen so far (the relative rank); you can pick only one candidate in the whole episode, and a candidate you pass over cannot be recalled.

zh: 选中全场最好的那个人的概率。
en: The probability of picking the best candidate overall.

zh:
**定理（Lindley 1961；Dynkin 1963）。** 在只依赖相对名次的规则里，使这个概率最大的是"先放过 $m^*$ 个人，之后遇到第一个比之前所有人都好的就要"。放过 $m\ge1$ 个人时，成功的概率是
$$P(m)=\frac mn\sum_{j=m}^{n-1}\frac1j,$$
$m^*$ 是使 $\sum_{j=m+1}^{n-1}\frac1j\le1$ 的最小的 $m$。$n\to\infty$ 时 $m^*/n\to1/e$，$P(m^*)\to1/e\approx0.368$。$n=100$ 时 $m^*=37$，$P=0.3710$。

**证明思路。** 第 $k$ 个人是全场最好的概率是 $1/n$；在这个条件下，规则选中他，当且仅当前 $k-1$ 个人里最好的那个落在前 $m$ 个里，概率是 $m/(k-1)$。对 $k=m+1,\dots,n$ 求和得到 $P(m)$。最优规则必是这种形式：只有"目前最好"的人才可能是全场最好；第 $k$ 个人是目前最好时，要他而成功的概率是 $k/n$，随 $k$ 递增，而放过他、之后按最优规则走的成功概率随 $k$ 递减，所以存在唯一的分界点，过了它就该要。
en:
**Theorem (Lindley 1961; Dynkin 1963).** Among rules that depend only on relative ranks, the one that maximizes this probability is "pass over the first $m^*$ candidates, then take the first one who is better than everyone before". When $m\ge1$ candidates are passed over, the probability of success is
$$P(m)=\frac mn\sum_{j=m}^{n-1}\frac1j,$$
and $m^*$ is the smallest $m$ for which $\sum_{j=m+1}^{n-1}\frac1j\le1$. As $n\to\infty$, $m^*/n\to1/e$ and $P(m^*)\to1/e\approx0.368$. For $n=100$, $m^*=37$ and $P=0.3710$.

**Proof sketch.** The probability that the $k$-th candidate is the best overall is $1/n$; given this, the rule picks that candidate if and only if the best of the first $k-1$ candidates falls among the first $m$, which has probability $m/(k-1)$. Summing over $k=m+1,\dots,n$ gives $P(m)$. The optimal rule must have this form: only a candidate who is "best so far" can be the best overall; when the $k$-th candidate is best so far, taking that candidate succeeds with probability $k/n$, which increases with $k$, while the success probability of passing and then following the optimal rule decreases with $k$, so there is a unique cutoff, and once past it you should take.

zh: 规则走到最后一个人还没出手的概率是 $m/(n-1)$，约 37%：这时只能要最后一个人，他的名次是随机的。所以把目标换成"名次越靠前越好"，它的期望名次约为 $n/5$，远不如名次门槛表（期望名次不到 4）。如果看得到分数、并且知道分数的分布，Gilbert–Mosteller 的门槛规则可以做到 0.58。真人实验里（Seale & Rapoport 1997），受试者平均停得比最优规则早。
en: The probability that the rule reaches the last candidate without having picked anyone is $m/(n-1)$, about 37%: it then has to take the last candidate, whose rank is random. So when the objective is changed to "The better the rank, the better", its expected rank is about $n/5$, far worse than the rank-threshold table (expected rank below 4). If the scores are visible and their distribution is known, the Gilbert–Mosteller threshold rule achieves 0.58. In experiments with human subjects (Seale & Rapoport 1997), subjects on average stopped earlier than the optimal rule.

zh: 对 $m$ 做扫描：得分曲线与图上的理论曲线 $P(m)$ 重合，峰值在 $n/e$ 附近，而且峰很平。把目标换成"名次"，同一条规则的最优 $m$ 大幅变小（约 $\sqrt n$ 的量级）。
en: Sweep $m$: the score curve coincides with the theoretical curve $P(m)$ on the chart; the peak is near $n/e$ and is very flat. Change the objective to "rank" and the optimal $m$ for the same rule becomes much smaller (roughly of order $\sqrt n$).

zh: 看得到分数、知道它服从 U(0,1) 时的最优规则：是目前最好的，并且分数高过一个随剩余人数下降的门槛，才要。
en: The optimal rule when the scores are visible and known to be U(0,1): take a candidate only if they are the best so far and their score is above a threshold that falls as fewer candidates remain.

zh: 分数独立同分布、服从 $U(0,1)$，并且你知道这一点（任何已知的连续分布都可以用它的分布函数变换成这种情形）。
en: The scores are i.i.d. $U(0,1)$, and you know this (any known continuous distribution can be transformed into this case by its distribution function).

zh: 选中全场最高分的概率。
en: The probability of picking the highest score overall.

zh:
**定理（Gilbert & Mosteller 1966）。** 最优规则是：眼前这个人是目前最高分，并且分数 $x\ge b_m$ 时要他，其中 $m$ 是身后还剩的人数，$b_0=0$，$b_m$（$m\ge1$）是方程
$$\sum_{j=1}^{m}\frac{b^{-j}-1}{j}=1$$
的唯一解。$b_1=\tfrac12$，$b_2\approx0.690$，$b_m\approx1-0.804/m$。成功的概率在 $n\to\infty$ 时趋于 $0.5802$，比只看名次的 $1/e$ 高得多。

**证明思路。** 身后还剩 $m$ 人、眼前是目前最高分 $x$。现在要他，成功的概率是 $x^m$（后面的人都比他低）。放过他、要下一个超过 $x$ 的人，成功的概率是 $\sum_{j=1}^{m}x^{j-1}\displaystyle\int_x^1y^{m-j}\,dy$。令两者相等，再除以 $x^m$，就得到上面的方程。问题属于"单调情形"：这个只往前看一步的比较给出的正是最优规则。
en:
**Theorem (Gilbert & Mosteller 1966).** The optimal rule is: take the current candidate when that candidate has the highest score so far and the score $x\ge b_m$, where $m$ is the number of candidates still to come, $b_0=0$, and for $m\ge1$ the equation
$$\sum_{j=1}^{m}\frac{b^{-j}-1}{j}=1$$
has a unique solution, which is $b_m$. This gives $b_1=\tfrac12$, $b_2\approx0.690$, $b_m\approx1-0.804/m$. The probability of success tends to $0.5802$ as $n\to\infty$, much higher than the $1/e$ attainable with ranks only.

**Proof sketch.** Suppose $m$ candidates are still to come and the current candidate has the highest score so far, $x$. Taking this candidate now succeeds with probability $x^m$ (everyone who follows scores lower). Passing and then taking the next candidate who exceeds $x$ succeeds with probability $\sum_{j=1}^{m}x^{j-1}\displaystyle\int_x^1y^{m-j}\,dy$. Setting the two equal and dividing by $x^m$ gives the equation above. The problem belongs to the "monotone case": this comparison, which looks only one step ahead, gives exactly the optimal rule.

zh: "只能和见过的人比"的设定下，裁判不把分数交给规则（$s.x$ 是 NaN），这张门槛表无从下手，只能一路放到最后一个人。目标换成"名次"时也不再最优。
en: In the "Compare only with those already seen" setting, the referee does not hand the scores to the rule ($s.x$ is NaN), so this threshold table has nothing to work with and can only pass all the way to the last candidate. It is also no longer optimal when the objective is changed to "rank".

zh: 设定选"看得到分数"、目标选"选中最好的"：得分约 0.58，明显高于先看后选的 0.37。把设定改回"只能和见过的人比"，它的得分掉到 $1/n$。
en: Choose the "Scores visible" setting and the "picking the best" objective: its score is about 0.58, clearly higher than the 0.37 of "Look, then leap". Change the setting back to "Compare only with those already seen" and its score drops to $1/n$.

zh: 目标是名次越靠前越好时的最优规则：越往后，可以接受的相对名次越宽。
en: The optimal rule when the objective is "The better the rank, the better": the later the candidate, the wider the range of relative ranks it accepts.

zh: 与经典设定相同：次序均匀随机，只看得到相对名次。
en: The same as the classical setting: the order is uniformly random, and only relative ranks are visible.

zh: 选中者最终名次（1 = 全场最好）的期望最小。
en: Minimize the expected final rank of the chosen candidate (1 = best overall).

zh:
**定理（Chow, Moriguti, Robbins & Samuels 1964）。** 关键事实：第 $i$ 个人的相对名次是 $j$ 时，他最终名次的期望是 $\dfrac{j\,(n+1)}{i+1}$。令 $c_i$ 为"放过第 $i$ 个人、之后按最优规则走"的期望名次，则
$$c_{n-1}=\frac{n+1}2,\qquad c_{i-1}=\frac1i\sum_{j=1}^{i}\min\Big(\frac{j\,(n+1)}{i+1},\ c_i\Big).$$
最优规则是：第 $i$ 个人的相对名次 $j\le s_i=\big\lfloor c_i\,(i+1)/(n+1)\big\rfloor$ 时要他。最优的期望名次 $c_0$ 随 $n$ 递增，极限是
$$\prod_{j=1}^{\infty}\Big(\frac{j+2}{j}\Big)^{1/(j+1)}\approx3.8695.$$
$n=100$ 时 $c_0\approx3.60$：从一百个人里选，平均能选到第三四名。整张表的计算量和存储量都是 $O(n)$。
en:
**Theorem (Chow, Moriguti, Robbins & Samuels 1964).** Key fact: when the $i$-th candidate has relative rank $j$, the expectation of that candidate's final rank is $\dfrac{j\,(n+1)}{i+1}$. Let $c_i$ be the expected rank from "passing over the $i$-th candidate and following the optimal rule from then on"; then
$$c_{n-1}=\frac{n+1}2,\qquad c_{i-1}=\frac1i\sum_{j=1}^{i}\min\Big(\frac{j\,(n+1)}{i+1},\ c_i\Big).$$
The optimal rule is: take the $i$-th candidate when the relative rank $j\le s_i=\big\lfloor c_i\,(i+1)/(n+1)\big\rfloor$. The optimal expected rank $c_0$ increases with $n$, and its limit is
$$\prod_{j=1}^{\infty}\Big(\frac{j+2}{j}\Big)^{1/(j+1)}\approx3.8695.$$
For $n=100$, $c_0\approx3.60$: choosing from one hundred candidates, on average you get the third or fourth best. The computation and the memory for the whole table are both $O(n)$.

zh: 目标是"选中最好的才算赢"时，它过早地接受了第二、第三名，成功率低于先看后选。看得到分数且知道分布时，还可以做得更好（那是 Robbins 问题，最优值至今未知）。
en: When the objective is "Only picking the best overall counts as a win", it accepts second- and third-ranked candidates too early, and its success rate is lower than that of "Look, then leap". When the scores are visible and their distribution is known, it is possible to do better still (that is Robbins' problem, and the optimal value is still unknown).

zh: 目标选"名次"：它的"选中者的平均名次"应约为 3.6（$n=100$），而先看后选约为 20。
en: Choose the "rank" objective: its "Average rank of the chosen candidate" should be about 3.6 ($n=100$), whereas for "Look, then leap" it is about 20.

zh: 分数不低于 1 − c/(身后人数 + c) 就要。不记历史。
en: Take the candidate if the score is at least 1 − c/(candidates still to come + c). It keeps no history.

zh: 门槛系数 c
en: Threshold coefficient c

zh: 分数独立同分布、服从 $U(0,1)$，并且你知道这一点。
en: The scores are i.i.d. $U(0,1)$, and you know this.

zh: 选中者最终名次的期望最小（看得到分数的版本，称为 Robbins 问题）。
en: Minimize the expected final rank of the chosen candidate (the version with visible scores, known as Robbins' problem).

zh:
**这是一个没有解决的问题。** 看得到分数时，最优规则要依赖全部历史，最优期望名次在 $n\to\infty$ 时的极限 $v$ 至今不知道确切值，只知道 $1.908<v<2.33$（下界来自 Bruss & Ferguson 1993；上界来自 Assaf & Samuel-Cahn 1996 的无记忆门槛规则，后来只被改进到小数点后第三位）。
这条规则属于"无记忆的门槛规则"：只看当前的分数和剩余人数。$c=2$ 时它的期望名次在 $n\to\infty$ 时约为 $2.33$，$n=100$ 时约为 $2.25$，已经比只看名次时的最优值 $3.60$ 好得多：绝对的分数里有名次没有的信息。
en:
**This is an unsolved problem.** When the scores are visible, the optimal rule depends on the entire history, and the exact value of the limit $v$ of the optimal expected rank as $n\to\infty$ is still unknown; all that is known is $1.908<v<2.33$ (the lower bound is from Bruss & Ferguson 1993; the upper bound comes from the memoryless threshold rules of Assaf & Samuel-Cahn 1996 and has since been improved only in the third decimal place).
This rule is one of the "memoryless threshold rules": it looks only at the current score and the number of candidates remaining. With $c=2$, its expected rank is about $2.33$ as $n\to\infty$ and about $2.25$ for $n=100$, already far better than $3.60$, the optimal value when only ranks are visible: absolute scores contain information that ranks do not.

zh: "只能和见过的人比"时裁判不给分数，它同样无从下手。目标是"选中最好的"时，它不要求"目前最好"，会要到不是最高分的人。
en: Under "Compare only with those already seen" the referee does not provide the scores, so it too has nothing to work with. When the objective is "picking the best", it does not require the candidate to be "best so far", so it will take candidates who do not have the highest score.

zh: 设定选"看得到分数"、目标选"名次"：对 $c$ 做扫描，峰值在 $c\approx1.5$–$2$，对应的平均名次约 2.2。
en: Choose the "Scores visible" setting and the "rank" objective: sweep $c$, and the peak is at $c\approx1.5$–$2$, with a corresponding average rank of about 2.2.

zh: 把本金原样带走。这套玩法的基准。
en: Take home the starting bankroll unchanged. The benchmark for this game.

zh: 不是最优：硬币偏向正面，每押 1 美元正面，期望盈利是 $2p-1>0$ 美元，不押等于放弃了这个优势。
en: Not optimal: the coin is biased toward heads, so every 1 dollar bet on heads has an expected profit of $2p-1>0$ dollars, and not betting gives up this edge.

zh: 只有 $p=\tfrac12$ 时不押才是对的（$p<\tfrac12$ 时该押反面；这套玩法里 $p$ 最小只能调到 $\tfrac12$）。
en: Not betting is right only when $p=\tfrac12$ (when $p<\tfrac12$ you should bet on tails; in this game $p$ cannot be set lower than $\tfrac12$).

zh: 得分恒等于本金。
en: The score always equals the starting bankroll.

zh: 每一次都押上手头资金的 f 倍，押正面。
en: On every flip, stake a fraction f of your current bankroll on heads.

zh: 押上的比例 f
en: Fraction staked f

zh: p = 0.6 时 Kelly 比例是 2p − 1 = 0.2
en: For p = 0.6 the Kelly fraction is 2p − 1 = 0.2

zh: 每一次独立，正面的概率 $p$ 已知，赔率 1:1。
en: The flips are independent, the probability of heads $p$ is known, and the payout is 1:1.

zh: Kelly 的目标是每次的对数增长率 $g(f)=p\ln(1+f)+(1-p)\ln(1-f)$；这套玩法实际打分的是期望到手金额 $\mathbb{E}\min(W_T,\text{封顶})$。两者不是一回事。
en: Kelly's objective is the log growth rate per flip, $g(f)=p\ln(1+f)+(1-p)\ln(1-f)$; what this game actually scores is the expected payout $\mathbb{E}\min(W_T,\text{cap})$. The two are not the same thing.

zh:
**定理（Kelly 1956）。** $g$ 在 $f^*=2p-1$ 处取最大值。$p=0.6$ 时 $f^*=0.2$，$g^*=0.0201$：不封顶地押 300 次，资金的中位数是 $25\,e^{300g^*}\approx10{,}500$ 美元，期望是 $25\times1.04^{300}\approx3.22\times10^{6}$ 美元（322 万）。
但这里有 250 美元的封顶和 300 次的期限，目标是期望到手金额，Kelly 比例并不是这个目标下的最优：封顶让"多赢"不值钱，最优打法比 Kelly 保守（见"动态规划"那条规则）。在固定比例这个族里，使期望到手金额最大的 $f$ 落在 $0.1$ 到 $0.2$ 之间，曲线很平：固定押 10%–20% 的人约 95% 能封顶，期望接近 240 美元。

**实验（Haghani & Dewey 2016）。** 61 名金融和经济专业的学生与年轻从业者，给 25 美元、半小时：28% 的人输光，只有 21% 的人拿到封顶，平均到手 91 美元；三分之二的人押过反面，18 人曾经一把全押。
en:
**Theorem (Kelly 1956).** $g$ attains its maximum at $f^*=2p-1$. For $p=0.6$, $f^*=0.2$ and $g^*=0.0201$: betting 300 times with no cap, the median bankroll is $25\,e^{300g^*}\approx10{,}500$ dollars and the expectation is $25\times1.04^{300}\approx3.22\times10^{6}$ dollars (3.22 million).
But here there is a cap of 250 dollars and a limit of 300 flips, and the objective is the expected payout, so the Kelly fraction is not optimal for this objective: the cap makes "winning more" worthless, and the optimal play is more conservative than Kelly (see the "Dynamic programming" rule). Within the fixed-fraction family, the $f$ that maximizes the expected payout lies between $0.1$ and $0.2$, and the curve is very flat: about 95% of those who bet a fixed 10%–20% reach the cap, and the expected payout is close to 240 dollars.

**Experiment (Haghani & Dewey 2016).** 61 students and young professionals in finance and economics were given 25 dollars and half an hour: 28% went broke, only 21% reached the cap, and the average payout was 91 dollars; two thirds bet on tails at some point, and 18 at some point bet everything on a single flip.

zh: $f$ 取大了，增长率转负：$g(f)=0$ 的点约在 $f=0.39$，再往上长期必输；$f=1$ 时第一次输就归零。$p$ 要靠估计时，高估优势就会押过头。
en: If $f$ is too large the growth rate turns negative: $g(f)=0$ at about $f=0.39$, and beyond that you are certain to lose in the long run; with $f=1$ the first loss takes you to zero. When $p$ has to be estimated, overestimating the edge leads to overbetting.

zh: 对 $f$ 做扫描：期望到手金额在 $0.1$–$0.2$ 之间是一段平台（约 240 美元），过了 $0.2$ 就开始下滑，越往右越快（$0.3$ 约 215，$0.4$ 约 174，$0.5$ 约 126 美元）；$f<0$（押反面）一路亏损。把封顶设为 0（不封顶）再看：期望到手金额变成由极少数大赢家决定的数，中位数才是该看的。
en: Sweep $f$: the expected payout is a plateau between $0.1$ and $0.2$ (about 240 dollars), starts to slide once past $0.2$, and falls faster the farther right you go (about 215 dollars at $0.3$, about 174 at $0.4$, about 126 at $0.5$); for $f<0$ (betting on tails) it loses money all the way. Set the cap to 0 (no cap) and look again: the expected payout becomes a number determined by a very few big winners, and the median is what you should look at.

zh: 把封顶和剩余次数都算进去，倒推每个时刻、每个资金水平下该押多少。
en: Account for both the cap and the number of flips left, and work backward to find how much to bet at every time and every bankroll level.

zh: 把资金分成多少格
en: Bankroll grid cells

zh: 格子越多越精细，计算量按平方增加
en: More cells give a finer grid; the computation grows as the square of their number

zh: 每一次独立，正面的概率 $p$ 已知；资金只取格点上的值（默认每格 1 美元）。
en: The flips are independent and the probability of heads $p$ is known; the bankroll takes values only on the grid points (by default each cell is 1 dollar).

zh: 期望到手金额 $\mathbb{E}\min(W_T,\text{封顶})$：正是这套玩法的计分方式。
en: The expected payout $\mathbb{E}\min(W_T,\text{cap})$: exactly the way this game is scored.

zh:
**在格点上精确最优（Bellman 方程）。** 令 $V_t(w)$ 为第 $t$ 次下注前资金为 $w$ 时的最优期望终值，
$$V_T(w)=w,\qquad V_t(w)=\max_{0\le b\le w}\Big[p\,V_{t+1}\big(\min(w+b,\text{封顶})\big)+(1-p)\,V_{t+1}(w-b)\Big].$$
倒推一遍就得到每个 $(t,w)$ 下的最优赌注。计算量是 $O(T\cdot G^2)$（$G$ 是格数），存储是 $O(T\cdot G)$；默认设置下约一千万次运算。
算出来的结论：在实验的设定下，最优打法的期望到手金额约 246 美元，高于 Kelly 的 237。它在开局时押得比 Kelly 小（时间充裕，没必要冒险），接近封顶时押得很小（时间还多的时候一两美元一注，比"刚好够到封顶"的数还少，只有最后几次才正好押到封顶所需），而在次数快用完、资金还差得远时，押得比 Kelly 大。目标函数一换，最优的下注方式就换了。
en:
**Exactly optimal on the grid (Bellman equation).** With $V_t(w)$ the optimal expected terminal wealth when the bankroll is $w$ before the $t$-th bet,
$$V_T(w)=w,\qquad V_t(w)=\max_{0\le b\le w}\Big[p\,V_{t+1}\big(\min(w+b,\text{cap})\big)+(1-p)\,V_{t+1}(w-b)\Big].$$
One backward pass gives the optimal bet at every $(t,w)$. The computation is $O(T\cdot G^2)$ ($G$ is the number of cells) and the memory is $O(T\cdot G)$; about ten million operations at the default settings.
What the computation shows: in the setting of the experiment, the optimal play has an expected payout of about 246 dollars, higher than Kelly's 237. It bets less than Kelly at the start (there is plenty of time, so no need to take risks) and bets very little near the cap (a dollar or two per bet while plenty of time remains, less than the amount that would "just reach the cap"; only in the last few flips does it bet exactly what is needed to reach the cap), whereas when the flips are nearly used up and the bankroll is still far short, it bets more than Kelly. Change the objective function and the optimal way to bet changes with it.

zh: $p$ 记错了，整张表就都错了；格子太粗时，小额赌注被舍入掉。不封顶时这个目标的最优解是每次全押（期望最大，但几乎肯定输光：不输光的概率只有 $p^T$），说明"期望到手金额"本身在不封顶时不是一个合理的目标。
en: If $p$ is wrong, the whole table is wrong; when the grid is too coarse, small bets are rounded away. With no cap, the optimal solution for this objective is to bet everything every time (the highest expectation, but almost certain to go broke: the probability of not going broke is only $p^T$), which shows that the "expected payout" is itself not a reasonable objective when there is no cap.

zh: 它的得分应高于任何固定比例；规则下方会显示倒推出的期望值和第一次的赌注。把次数改成 30：时间不够了，最优赌注明显变大。
en: Its score should be higher than that of any fixed fraction; below the rule, the expected value obtained by backward induction and the first bet are displayed. Change the number of flips to 30: time is now short, and the optimal bets become clearly larger.

zh: 从一个小注开始，输一次就把注码翻倍，赢一次回到起始注码。
en: Start with a small bet, double the bet after every loss, and go back to the starting bet after every win.

zh: 起始注码（美元）
en: Starting bet (dollars)

zh: "连输总有个头，赢一把就全回来了。"
en: "A losing streak has to end sometime, and one win brings it all back."

zh: 没有显式目标：它让每一轮"以赢告终"的概率很高，每轮只赢一个起始注码。
en: There is no explicit objective: it makes each cycle very likely to "end with a win", and each cycle wins only one starting bet.

zh: 不是最优。每一次的期望盈利是 $(2p-1)\times$ 赌注，与怎么安排注码无关；加倍只是把很多次小赢和一次大输捆在一起。连输 $k$ 次需要的赌注是 $2^k$ 个起始注码，资金有限，迟早押不起：即使硬币偏向你（$p=0.6$），25 美元本金、1 美元起注，也有大约三分之一的局以输光告终。
en: Not optimal. The expected profit of every flip is $(2p-1)\times$ the bet, no matter how the bets are sized; doubling only bundles many small wins together with one big loss. After $k$ losses in a row the bet required is $2^k$ starting bets, and since the bankroll is finite, sooner or later you cannot cover it: even with the coin biased in your favor ($p=0.6$), with a 25-dollar starting bankroll and a 1-dollar starting bet, about one third of episodes end broke.

zh: 任何时候都可能：连输的概率 $(1-p)^k$ 随 $k$ 指数下降，但需要的赌注指数上升，两者相乘并不小。
en: It can fail at any time: the probability $(1-p)^k$ of a losing streak falls exponentially in $k$, but the bet required rises exponentially, and their product is not small.

zh: 看"输光的比例"：它远高于固定押 20%（后者几乎为 0）。在终值分布图上，它是两头堆：一堆在 0，一堆在两百美元上下。
en: Look at "Share of episodes ending broke": it is far higher than for a fixed 20% bet (where it is almost 0). In the terminal wealth distribution chart, it piles up at both ends: one pile at 0 and one pile around two hundred dollars.

zh: 平时押正面，连出 k 次正面之后改押反面。
en: Normally bet on heads; after k heads in a row, switch to betting on tails.

zh: 连出几次正面后改押反面
en: Heads in a row before switching to tails

zh: "连着出了这么多次正面，下一次该轮到反面了。"（赌徒谬误）
en: "After so many heads in a row, tails is due next." (the gambler's fallacy)

zh: 不是最优，而且有害。各次独立，连出多少次正面，下一次正面的概率还是 $p$。押反面的每一次，期望盈利是 $-(2p-1)\times$ 赌注：把自己的优势反过来送给了对方。实验里 61 人中有 41 人（67%）押过反面，29 人押了五次以上。
en: Not optimal, and harmful as well. The flips are independent: no matter how many heads have come up in a row, the probability of heads on the next flip is still $p$. Every bet on tails has an expected profit of $-(2p-1)\times$ the bet: you turn your own edge around and hand it to the other side. In the experiment, 41 of the 61 subjects (67%) bet on tails at some point, and 29 did so more than five times.

zh: 只要硬币偏向正面，它就比一直押正面差。
en: As long as the coin is biased toward heads, it does worse than always betting on heads.

zh: 对 $k$ 做扫描：$k$ 越小，押反面的次数越多，得分越低；$k$ 很大时几乎不触发，得分回到固定比例的水平。
en: Sweep $k$: the smaller $k$ is, the more often it bets on tails and the lower the score; when $k$ is large it almost never triggers, and the score returns to the level of the fixed fraction.

zh: 每一把都押固定的一小注。这套玩法的基准。
en: Stake the same small amount on every bet. The benchmark for this game.

zh: 每把押多少（目标 = 1）
en: Stake per bet (target = 1)

zh: "押小一点，稳一点。"
en: "Bet a little smaller, play a little safer."

zh: 到达目标的概率。
en: The probability of reaching the target.

zh:
**赌徒破产公式。** 资金是赌注的 $i$ 倍、目标是 $N$ 倍，每把胜率 $p\ne\tfrac12$，则到达目标的概率是
$$\frac{1-r^{\,i}}{1-r^{\,N}},\qquad r=\frac{1-p}{p}.$$
不利赌局里（$p<\tfrac12$，$r>1$），赌注越小，$i$ 和 $N$ 越大，这个概率越小：轮盘押红黑（$p=18/38$）、要把钱翻倍时，每把押目标的 5% 是 $25.9\%$，押 1% 只剩 $0.5\%$。押得越小、把数越多，大数定律越有机会把那一点劣势兑现出来。在不利赌局里它是最差的打法之一。
有利赌局里（$p>\tfrac12$）结论反过来：赌注越小越好，概率趋于 1。
en:
**The gambler's ruin formula.** If the bankroll is $i$ times the stake and the target is $N$ times the stake, and each bet wins with probability $p\ne\tfrac12$, then the probability of reaching the target is
$$\frac{1-r^{\,i}}{1-r^{\,N}},\qquad r=\frac{1-p}{p}.$$
In an unfavorable game ($p<\tfrac12$, $r>1$), the smaller the stake, the larger $i$ and $N$ are and the smaller this probability is: betting on red or black at roulette ($p=18/38$) and trying to double your money, staking 5% of the target per bet gives $25.9\%$, and staking 1% leaves only $0.5\%$. The smaller the stakes and the more bets there are, the more opportunity the law of large numbers has to make that small disadvantage materialize. In an unfavorable game it is one of the worst ways to play.
In a favorable game ($p>\tfrac12$) the conclusion is reversed: the smaller the stake the better, and the probability tends to 1.

zh: $p<\tfrac12$ 时。另外把数有上限时，小注可能来不及分出结果：公式不限把数，而这里到了上限还没到目标就算失败。
en: When $p<\tfrac12$. Also, when the number of bets is limited, small stakes may not have time to produce an outcome: the formula puts no limit on the number of bets, whereas here reaching the limit without reaching the target counts as failure.

zh: 对赌注做扫描：注码不小于目标的 5% 时，得分贴着图上的赌徒破产公式（注码能把起始资金和"离目标的距离"都整除时两者一致；除不尽时最后一把押不满，公式是近似的：默认设定下差不到 1 个百分点，胜率离 $\tfrac12$ 越远差得越多，胜率 0.4 时能差 3 个百分点）；更小的注在 500 把里分不出胜负，实验点落在曲线下方。把胜率调到 0.55、"最多押多少把"调到 4000，曲线的方向反过来。
en: Sweep the stake: when the stake is at least 5% of the target, the score hugs the gambler's ruin formula on the chart (the two agree when the stake divides both the starting bankroll and the "distance to the target" evenly; when it does not, the last bet cannot be a full stake and the formula is approximate: under the default settings the difference is less than 1 percentage point, it grows the farther the win probability is from $\tfrac12$, and at a win probability of 0.4 it can be 3 percentage points); smaller stakes cannot settle the outcome within 500 bets, and the experimental points fall below the curve. Set the win probability to 0.55 and "Maximum number of bets" to 4000, and the direction of the curve reverses.

zh: 每一把都押上刚好够到目标的数额，够不着就全押。
en: On every bet, stake exactly the amount needed to reach the target; if you cannot reach it, stake everything.

zh: 每一把独立，胜率 $p\le\tfrac12$（公平或不利），赔率 1:1；每把可以押不超过手头资金的任意数额；不限把数。
en: The bets are independent, with win probability $p\le\tfrac12$ (fair or unfavorable) and a 1:1 payout; on each bet you may stake any amount up to your current bankroll; the number of bets is unlimited.

zh: 到达目标的概率 $Q(x)$，$x$ 是手头资金占目标的比例。
en: The probability $Q(x)$ of reaching the target, where $x$ is the current bankroll as a fraction of the target.

zh:
**定理（Dubins & Savage 1965）。** 胜率 $p\le\tfrac12$ 的红黑赌局里，大胆下注（资金 $x\le\tfrac12$ 时全押，$x>\tfrac12$ 时押 $1-x$）使到达目标的概率最大。它的成功概率满足
$$Q(x)=p\,Q(2x)\ \ (x\le\tfrac12),\qquad Q(x)=p+(1-p)\,Q(2x-1)\ \ (x\ge\tfrac12).$$
$x=\tfrac12$ 时一把定输赢，$Q=p$。$p<\tfrac12$ 时 $Q$ 连续、严格递增，却几乎处处导数为 0：它是"二进制各位独立、每位为 0 的概率是 $p$"的随机数的分布函数（Lebesgue 奇异函数）。

**直觉。** 结局只有 0 和 1 两种，所以到达目标的概率等于期末资金的期望，也就是 $x-(1-2p)\times$ 押出去的总金额的期望。不利赌局里要让这个概率大，就该让押出去的总金额尽量少。公平赌局（$p=\tfrac12$）里资金是有界鞅，由可选停时定理 $\mathbb{E}[W_\tau]=x$，所以任何打法到达目标的概率都不超过 $x$；在把数用完之前几乎必然分出胜负的打法，恰好等于 $x$。
en:
**Theorem (Dubins & Savage 1965).** In a red-and-black game with win probability $p\le\tfrac12$, bold play (stake everything when the bankroll $x\le\tfrac12$, stake $1-x$ when $x>\tfrac12$) maximizes the probability of reaching the target. Its success probability satisfies
$$Q(x)=p\,Q(2x)\ \ (x\le\tfrac12),\qquad Q(x)=p+(1-p)\,Q(2x-1)\ \ (x\ge\tfrac12).$$
At $x=\tfrac12$ a single bet decides everything, and $Q=p$. For $p<\tfrac12$, $Q$ is continuous and strictly increasing, yet its derivative is 0 almost everywhere: it is the distribution function of a random number "whose binary digits are independent, each equal to 0 with probability $p$" (Lebesgue's singular function).

**Intuition.** There are only two outcomes, 0 and 1, so the probability of reaching the target equals the expected final bankroll, which is $x-(1-2p)\times$ the expected total amount staked. To make this probability large in an unfavorable game, the total amount staked should be as small as possible. In a fair game ($p=\tfrac12$) the bankroll is a bounded martingale, and the optional stopping theorem gives $\mathbb{E}[W_\tau]=x$, so no way of playing reaches the target with probability greater than $x$; any way of playing that almost surely settles the outcome before the bets run out attains exactly $x$.

zh: $p>\tfrac12$ 时它不是最优：那时应该押小注，让优势靠次数兑现。目标换成"长期增长率"时，全押意味着第一次输就归零。
en: For $p>\tfrac12$ it is not optimal: in that case you should stake small amounts and let the edge be realized over many bets. If the objective is changed to "Long-run growth rate", staking everything means the first loss takes you to zero.

zh: 把起始资金比例从 0.1 扫到 0.9（改玩法的参数）：成功率落在 $Q(x)$ 上。与"小注慢磨"比：$p=18/38$、翻倍时是 $47.4\%$ 对公式给出的 $0.5\%$；500 把的上限下，每把押 1% 的实测值还要低，只有千分之一上下。
en: Sweep the starting bankroll as a fraction of the target from 0.1 to 0.9 (by changing the game's parameter): the success rate falls on $Q(x)$. Compare with "Small bets, slowly": for $p=18/38$ and doubling, it is $47.4\%$ against the $0.5\%$ given by the formula; under the 500-bet limit, the measured value for staking 1% per bet is lower still, only about one in a thousand.

zh: 每一把押上手头资金的 f 倍。
en: On every bet, stake a fraction f of your current bankroll.

zh: 每一把独立，赔率 1:1。
en: The bets are independent, with a 1:1 payout.

zh: 不是最优（$p\le\tfrac12$ 时）：由 Dubins–Savage 定理，任何打法都不超过大胆下注。按比例下注的资金永远不会恰好归零，但会越缩越小，在把数上限之前到不了目标。$f=1$ 时，裁判把赌注限制在"够到目标"以内，它就是大胆下注。
en: Not optimal (when $p\le\tfrac12$): by the Dubins–Savage theorem, no way of playing does better than bold play. With proportional betting the bankroll never falls exactly to zero, but it keeps shrinking and cannot reach the target before the limit on the number of bets. When $f=1$, the referee limits the stake to what is "enough to reach the target", so it is bold play.

zh: $f$ 小时与小注慢磨同病：把数太多。
en: When $f$ is small it has the same flaw as "Small bets, slowly": too many bets.

zh: 对 $f$ 做扫描：不利赌局里得分随 $f$ 上升，在 $f=1$ 处到达大胆下注的水平。
en: Sweep $f$: in an unfavorable game the score rises with $f$ and reaches the level of bold play at $f=1$.

zh: 每回合等可能地挑一台。这套玩法的基准。
en: Each round, pick an arm uniformly at random. The benchmark for this game.

zh: 没有优化目标：纯粹的"探索"，完全不利用学到的东西。
en: There is no optimization objective: pure "exploration", with no exploitation at all of what has been learned.

zh: 不是最优。每回合的期望得分是各台中奖率的平均数；遗憾（与一直拉最好那台相比少拿的分）随回合数线性增长。
en: Not optimal. The expected score per round is the average of the arms' win probabilities; the regret (the points lost compared with always pulling the best arm) grows linearly with the number of rounds.

zh: 始终如此：它从不利用已经学到的东西。
en: Always: it never exploits what it has already learned.

zh: 得分约等于各台中奖率的平均（中奖率从 $U(0,1)$ 里抽时是 0.5）。
en: The score is approximately the average of the arms' win probabilities (0.5 when the win probabilities are drawn from $U(0,1)$).

zh: 每台先拉一次，之后永远拉目前平均回报最高的那台。
en: Pull each arm once, then always pull the arm with the highest average reward so far.

zh: "眼下看起来最好的，就是最好的。"
en: "Whatever looks best right now is the best."

zh: 每一回合都最大化眼前的估计值：纯粹的"利用"，不再探索。
en: Maximize the current estimate in every round: pure "exploitation", with no more exploration.

zh:
不是最优：遗憾随回合数**线性**增长。原因是它会以正的概率永远认错：最好的那台只要开头运气差（比如第一次没中，估计值是 0），就再也不会被拉到，错误永远得不到纠正。
它的平均成绩看上去不差，是因为多数时候它碰巧认对了；看遗憾的分布，会发现少数局里遗憾特别大。
en:
Not optimal: the regret grows **linearly** with the number of rounds. The reason is that with positive probability it stays wrong forever: if the best arm is unlucky at the start (for example, its first pull is a miss, so its estimate is 0), it is never pulled again, and the mistake is never corrected.
Its average result does not look bad because most of the time it happens to pick the right arm; look at the distribution of regret and you will find a few episodes in which the regret is especially large.

zh: 各台的中奖率接近时（需要很多次才能分辨），以及回合数很多时（认错的代价按回合数放大）。
en: When the arms' win probabilities are close to each other (it takes many pulls to tell them apart), and when there are many rounds (the cost of picking the wrong arm scales with the number of rounds).

zh: 把一局的次数从 500 调到 5000，看"累计遗憾"：Thompson 抽样从 14 上下到 25 上下，UCB1 从 48 到 137（都不到 3 倍，对数增长），贪心从 25 上下到 210 以上（八九倍，线性增长）。
en: Raise the number of pulls per episode from 500 to 5000 and look at "Cumulative regret": Thompson sampling goes from about 14 to about 25, UCB1 from 48 to 137 (both by less than a factor of 3, logarithmic growth), and greedy from about 25 to more than 210 (by a factor of eight or nine, linear growth).

zh: 大多数时候拉目前最好的，每回合留 ε 的概率随便试一台。
en: Most of the time pull the arm that is best so far; each round, with probability ε, try an arm at random.

zh: 试探的概率 ε
en: Exploration probability ε

zh: 各台的回报独立同分布，中奖率不随时间变。
en: Each arm's rewards are i.i.d., and the win probabilities do not change over time.

zh: 在"利用眼下最好的"和"继续试探"之间，用一个固定的比例折中。
en: A compromise, in a fixed proportion, between "exploiting what looks best right now" and "continuing to explore".

zh: 固定的 $\varepsilon$ 不是最优：试探永不停止，遗憾仍然线性增长，斜率约为 $\varepsilon\times$（平均差距）；但它不会像贪心那样永远认错。让 $\varepsilon_t$ 按 $1/t$ 的速度下降，可以把遗憾降到 $O(\ln T)$（Auer, Cesa-Bianchi & Fischer 2002），不过下降的系数要用到各台之间的差距，而差距事先并不知道。
en: A fixed $\varepsilon$ is not optimal: the exploration never stops, so the regret still grows linearly, with slope about $\varepsilon\times$ (the average gap); but it does not stay wrong forever the way greedy does. Letting $\varepsilon_t$ decrease at the rate $1/t$ brings the regret down to $O(\ln T)$ (Auer, Cesa-Bianchi & Fischer 2002), but the coefficient of the decrease depends on the gaps between the arms, and the gaps are not known in advance.

zh: $\varepsilon$ 大了浪费回合，小了发现最好的那台太慢；最优的 $\varepsilon$ 依赖回合数和差距。
en: If $\varepsilon$ is too large it wastes rounds; if it is too small it is too slow to find the best arm; the optimal $\varepsilon$ depends on the number of rounds and on the gaps.

zh: 对 $\varepsilon$ 做扫描：得分是单峰的，峰很靠左。只拉 50 次时最好的是 $\varepsilon=0$（没有时间探索）；500 次以上，峰在 $0.02$ 到 $0.03$ 之间，次数再多也不怎么动。默认的扫描每 $0.05$ 取一个点，图上的峰落在 $0$ 或 $0.05$；把范围缩到 $0$ 到 $0.1$ 再扫一遍才看得清。默认的 $\varepsilon=0.1$ 偏大。
en: Sweep $\varepsilon$: the score has a single peak, far to the left. With only 50 pulls the best value is $\varepsilon=0$ (there is no time to explore); with 500 pulls or more the peak is between $0.02$ and $0.03$, and it hardly moves when the number of pulls grows further. The default sweep takes a point every $0.05$, so the peak on the chart falls at $0$ or $0.05$; narrow the range to between $0$ and $0.1$ and sweep again to see it clearly. The default $\varepsilon=0.1$ is on the large side.

zh: 每台轮流拉 m 次，然后认准平均回报最高的那台拉到底。
en: Pull each arm m times in turn, then commit to the arm with the highest average reward and pull it to the end.

zh: 每台先试几次 m
en: Trial pulls per arm m

zh: 各台的回报独立同分布；总回合数 $T$ 事先知道。
en: Each arm's rewards are i.i.d.; the total number of rounds $T$ is known in advance.

zh: 先用固定的预算做试验，再把结论用到底：A/B 测试的做法。
en: Experiment first with a fixed budget, then apply the conclusion to the end: the A/B testing approach.

zh: 两台机器、回报在 $[0,1]$ 内、差距为 $\Delta$ 时，试探阶段的代价是 $m\Delta$，认错的概率不超过 $e^{-m\Delta^2}$（Hoeffding 不等式），认错的代价不超过 $T\Delta$。若知道 $\Delta$，取 $m\approx\dfrac{1}{\Delta^2}\ln(T\Delta^2)$ 可使遗憾为 $O(\ln T/\Delta)$（教科书里常见的 $e^{-m\Delta^2/4}$ 和 $m\approx\frac{4}{\Delta^2}\ln\frac{T\Delta^2}{4}$ 是噪声方差为 1 时的写法）；不知道 $\Delta$ 时，取 $m\propto T^{2/3}$，最坏情形的遗憾是 $O(T^{2/3})$，比 UCB 和 Thompson 抽样的 $O(\sqrt{T\ln T})$ 差。
en: With two arms, rewards in $[0,1]$ and a gap of $\Delta$, the exploration phase costs $m\Delta$, the probability of committing to the wrong arm is at most $e^{-m\Delta^2}$ (Hoeffding's inequality), and the cost of committing to the wrong arm is at most $T\Delta$. If $\Delta$ is known, taking $m\approx\dfrac{1}{\Delta^2}\ln(T\Delta^2)$ makes the regret $O(\ln T/\Delta)$ (the forms $e^{-m\Delta^2/4}$ and $m\approx\frac{4}{\Delta^2}\ln\frac{T\Delta^2}{4}$ common in textbooks are written for noise variance 1); if $\Delta$ is not known, taking $m\propto T^{2/3}$ gives a worst-case regret of $O(T^{2/3})$, worse than the $O(\sqrt{T\ln T})$ of UCB and Thompson sampling.

zh: 试探的预算是事先定死的：差距大时试多了，差距小时试少了。认定之后不再看数据，错了也改不过来。
en: The exploration budget is fixed in advance: it explores too much when the gap is large and too little when the gap is small. After committing it no longer looks at the data, so a wrong choice cannot be corrected.

zh: 对 $m$ 做扫描：单峰。把各台的中奖率设成"都在 0.4 到 0.6 之间"，最优的 $m$ 明显变大。
en: Sweep $m$: a single peak. Set the arms' win probabilities to "All between 0.4 and 0.6" and the optimal $m$ becomes clearly larger.

zh: 给每台的平均回报加上一个不确定性奖励，拉加完之后最高的那台。
en: Add an uncertainty bonus to each arm's average reward, and pull the arm with the highest total.

zh: 探索系数 c
en: Exploration coefficient c

zh: 标准的 UCB1 是 c = 2；实际常取更小的值
en: Standard UCB1 uses c = 2; in practice smaller values are common

zh: 各台的回报在 $[0,1]$ 内，独立同分布，均值不随时间变。
en: Each arm's rewards lie in $[0,1]$ and are i.i.d., with a mean that does not change over time.

zh: 期望遗憾 $R_T=T\mu^*-\mathbb{E}\sum_{t\le T}\mu_{a_t}$ 尽量小，$\mu^*$ 是最好那台的均值。
en: Make the expected regret $R_T=T\mu^*-\mathbb{E}\sum_{t\le T}\mu_{a_t}$ as small as possible, where $\mu^*$ is the mean of the best arm.

zh:
**定理（Auer, Cesa-Bianchi & Fischer 2002）。** 每回合拉指数 $\bar x_k+\sqrt{\dfrac{2\ln t}{n_k}}$ 最大的那台（$\bar x_k$ 是第 $k$ 台的平均回报，$n_k$ 是它被拉过的次数），则对任意 $T$，
$$R_T\le8\sum_{k:\Delta_k>0}\frac{\ln T}{\Delta_k}+\Big(1+\frac{\pi^2}{3}\Big)\sum_k\Delta_k,\qquad\Delta_k=\mu^*-\mu_k.$$
**下界（Lai & Robbins 1985）。** 任何"对所有问题都不太差"的规则都满足 $\liminf R_T/\ln T\ge\sum_{k:\Delta_k>0}\Delta_k/\mathrm{KL}(\mu_k,\mu^*)$。所以对数增长是最好的可能，UCB1 达到了这个阶，只是常数不是最优的。

**想法。** "乐观地面对不确定性"：指数是均值的一个置信上界（Hoeffding 不等式）。一台机器被拉到，要么因为它确实好，要么因为我们对它了解得太少；后一种情形每发生一次，不确定性就缩小一点。每一步的计算量是 $O(K)$，存储是 $O(K)$。
en:
**Theorem (Auer, Cesa-Bianchi & Fischer 2002).** If in each round you pull the arm with the largest index $\bar x_k+\sqrt{\dfrac{2\ln t}{n_k}}$ ($\bar x_k$ is the average reward of arm $k$ and $n_k$ is the number of times it has been pulled), then for every $T$,
$$R_T\le8\sum_{k:\Delta_k>0}\frac{\ln T}{\Delta_k}+\Big(1+\frac{\pi^2}{3}\Big)\sum_k\Delta_k,\qquad\Delta_k=\mu^*-\mu_k.$$
**Lower bound (Lai & Robbins 1985).** Every rule that is "not too bad on any problem" satisfies $\liminf R_T/\ln T\ge\sum_{k:\Delta_k>0}\Delta_k/\mathrm{KL}(\mu_k,\mu^*)$. So logarithmic growth is the best possible, and UCB1 attains this order; only its constant is not optimal.

**Idea.** "Optimism in the face of uncertainty": the index is an upper confidence bound on the mean (Hoeffding's inequality). An arm gets pulled either because it really is good or because we know too little about it; each time the latter happens, the uncertainty shrinks a little. Each step takes $O(K)$ computation and $O(K)$ memory.

zh: $c=2$ 是为了证明而取的保守值：回合数不多时探索过头，实际成绩往往不如 Thompson 抽样，甚至不如贪心。均值随时间变化时，旧数据会误导它。
en: $c=2$ is a conservative value chosen for the sake of the proof: when there are not many rounds it explores too much, and in practice it often does worse than Thompson sampling, or even worse than greedy. When the means change over time, old data mislead it.

zh: 对 $c$ 做扫描：500 回合时最优值在 $0.1$ 上下（$0.05$ 到 $0.2$ 之间，得分约 $0.81$），远小于 2；$c=2$ 时只有 $0.74$。把一局的次数调到 5000，标准的 $c=2$ 和贪心的差距反过来，贪心被甩开。
en: Sweep $c$: with 500 rounds the best value is around $0.1$ (between $0.05$ and $0.2$, score about $0.81$), far below 2; at $c=2$ the score is only $0.74$. Raise the number of pulls per episode to 5000 and the gap between the standard $c=2$ and the greedy rule reverses: greedy is left behind.

zh: 对每台的中奖率保持一个后验分布，每回合各抽一个数，拉抽出来最大的那台。
en: Keep a posterior distribution for each arm's win probability; each round, draw one number from each posterior and pull the arm with the largest draw.

zh: 每台机器的回报是伯努利分布，中奖率的先验是 $U(0,1)$，即 $\mathrm{Beta}(1,1)$。
en: Each arm's reward is Bernoulli; the prior on its win probability is $U(0,1)$, that is, $\mathrm{Beta}(1,1)$.

zh: 期望遗憾尽量小（或者贝叶斯意义下的期望总回报尽量大）。
en: Make the expected regret as small as possible (or, in the Bayesian sense, the expected total reward as large as possible).

zh:
**算法（Thompson 1933）。** 中了 $w$ 次、没中 $l$ 次之后，中奖率的后验是 $\mathrm{Beta}(1+w,\,1+l)$。每回合从每台的后验里各抽一个数，拉最大的那台：一台机器被选中的概率，正好等于"它是最好的那台"的后验概率。

**定理（Kaufmann, Korda & Munos 2012；Agrawal & Goyal 2013）。** 对伯努利老虎机，Thompson 抽样的遗憾满足
$$\limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac{R_T}{\ln T}\le\sum_{k:\Delta_k>0}\frac{\Delta_k}{\mathrm{KL}(\mu_k,\mu^*)},$$
恰好达到 Lai–Robbins 下界：它是渐近最优的，连常数都对。
严格的贝叶斯最优解是 Gittins 指数（Gittins 1979，针对带折现的无限期问题），计算要复杂得多；Thompson 抽样每一步只要 $O(K)$ 次抽样、$O(K)$ 的存储。Thompson 1933 年提出它时，想的是临床试验：怎样在试验过程中就让更多的病人用上更可能有效的疗法。
en:
**Algorithm (Thompson 1933).** After $w$ wins and $l$ misses, the posterior of the win probability is $\mathrm{Beta}(1+w,\,1+l)$. Each round, draw one number from each arm's posterior and pull the arm with the largest draw: the probability that an arm is chosen is exactly the posterior probability that "it is the best arm".

**Theorem (Kaufmann, Korda & Munos 2012; Agrawal & Goyal 2013).** For Bernoulli bandits, the regret of Thompson sampling satisfies
$$\limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac{R_T}{\ln T}\le\sum_{k:\Delta_k>0}\frac{\Delta_k}{\mathrm{KL}(\mu_k,\mu^*)},$$
which matches the Lai–Robbins lower bound exactly: it is asymptotically optimal, down to the constant.
The exact Bayes-optimal solution is the Gittins index (Gittins 1979, for the discounted infinite-horizon problem), which is far more complicated to compute; Thompson sampling needs only $O(K)$ draws and $O(K)$ memory per step. When Thompson proposed it in 1933, he had clinical trials in mind: how to get more patients onto the treatment more likely to work while the trial is still under way.

zh: 先验与真实情况相差很远、而数据又少时，先验的影响会持续一段时间。回报不是 0/1 时要换后验的分布族。
en: When the prior is far from the truth and data are scarce, the influence of the prior lasts for a while. When rewards are not 0/1, a different family of posterior distributions is needed.

zh: 默认设定下、各条规则都取默认参数时，它的遗憾是内置规则里最小的（把 UCB 的 $c$ 调到 0.1 上下，UCB 的遗憾还能再小一点：约 11 对 14）。它用到了随机数，但每一局的随机数序列是固定的，结果可以复现。
en: Under the default settings, with every rule at its default parameters, its regret is the smallest among the built-in rules (tuning UCB's $c$ to around 0.1 makes UCB's regret a little smaller still: about 11 versus 14). It uses random numbers, but the random-number sequence of each episode is fixed, so the results are reproducible.

zh: 每天都订到目前为止需求的平均值。这套玩法的基准。
en: Every day, order the average of demand so far. The benchmark for this game.

zh: "需求平均是多少，就订多少。"
en: "Order whatever demand is on average."

zh: 让订货量与需求的平方差最小，而不是利润最大。
en: It minimizes the squared difference between the order quantity and demand instead of maximizing profit.

zh: 一般不是最优。利润对"订多了"和"订少了"的惩罚不一样：少订一件，少赚 $r-c$（售价减进价）；多订一件，亏 $c-v$（进价减残值）。均值是最优订货量，当且仅当它恰好落在临界分位数上：$F(\mathbb{E}D)=\dfrac{r-c}{r-v}$。两种代价相等（临界分位为 $\tfrac12$）而分布对称，是最常见的例子；代价不对称时，一般就不是了。
en: Not optimal in general. Profit penalizes "ordering too much" and "ordering too little" differently: one unit too few earns $r-c$ less (selling price minus unit cost); one unit too many loses $c-v$ (unit cost minus salvage value). The mean is the optimal order quantity if and only if it sits exactly at the critical-fractile quantile: $F(\mathbb{E}D)=\dfrac{r-c}{r-v}$. Equal costs (critical fractile $\tfrac12$) together with a symmetric distribution is the most common example; when the costs are asymmetric, it generally is not.

zh: 利润越偏离"多一件、少一件代价相同"，它丢得越多：高利润的商品它订少了，低利润的商品它订多了。
en: The further the margins are from "one unit too many and one unit too few cost the same", the more it loses: it orders too little of high-margin goods and too much of low-margin goods.

zh: 把进价从 3 改成 9（售价 12）：它在两种情形下订的量几乎一样，而最优订货量从 225 变成了 76。
en: Change the unit cost from 3 to 9 (selling price 12): it orders almost the same quantity in both cases, while the optimal order quantity goes from 225 to 76.

zh: 每天都订 q 件。
en: Order q units every day.

zh: 订货量 q
en: Order quantity q

zh: 每天的需求独立同分布。
en: Daily demand is i.i.d.

zh: 每天的期望利润 $\pi(q)=(r-v)\,\mathbb{E}\min(q,D)-(c-v)\,q$，其中 $r$ 是售价，$c$ 是进价，$v$ 是残值，$D$ 是需求。
en: Expected daily profit $\pi(q)=(r-v)\,\mathbb{E}\min(q,D)-(c-v)\,q$, where $r$ is the selling price, $c$ the unit cost, $v$ the salvage value and $D$ the demand.

zh:
需求独立同分布、货不能留到明天，每天面对的是同一个问题，所以最优的规则就是一个常数 $q^*$。**定理（临界分位；Arrow, Harris & Marschak 1951）。** $\pi$ 是凹函数，
$$\pi'(q)=(r-v)\,\mathbb{P}(D>q)-(c-v)=0\iff F(q^*)=\frac{r-c}{r-v}.$$
记少订一件的损失为 $c_u=r-c$，多订一件的损失为 $c_o=c-v$，则 $F(q^*)=\dfrac{c_u}{c_u+c_o}$：订到"够卖（不缺货）的概率"等于这个比值为止；卖光的概率是剩下的 $\dfrac{c_o}{c_u+c_o}$。需求 $U(1,300)$、售价 12、进价 3 时，临界分位是 $0.75$，$q^*\approx225$：四天里有三天够卖。
en:
Demand is i.i.d. and goods cannot be carried over to the next day, so every day poses the same problem and the optimal rule is a constant $q^*$. **Theorem (critical fractile; Arrow, Harris & Marschak 1951).** The function $\pi$ is concave, and
$$\pi'(q)=(r-v)\,\mathbb{P}(D>q)-(c-v)=0\iff F(q^*)=\frac{r-c}{r-v}.$$
Write $c_u=r-c$ for the loss from ordering one unit too few and $c_o=c-v$ for the loss from ordering one unit too many; then $F(q^*)=\dfrac{c_u}{c_u+c_o}$: order until "the probability of having enough to sell (no stockout)" equals this ratio; the probability of selling out is the remaining $\dfrac{c_o}{c_u+c_o}$. With demand $U(1,300)$, selling price 12 and unit cost 3, the critical fractile is $0.75$ and $q^*\approx225$: enough to sell on three days out of four.

zh: 分布未知时 $q^*$ 要靠估计；需求有趋势或季节性时，常数不再合适。
en: When the distribution is unknown, $q^*$ has to be estimated; when demand has a trend or seasonality, a constant is no longer appropriate.

zh: 对 $q$ 做扫描：得分与图上的理论曲线 $\pi(q)$ 重合，峰值在 $q^*$。曲线在峰值两侧不对称：高利润的商品，少订比多订亏得多。
en: Sweep $q$: the score coincides with the theoretical curve $\pi(q)$ on the chart, with its peak at $q^*$. The curve is asymmetric about the peak: for a high-margin good, ordering too little costs far more than ordering too much.

zh: 知道需求的分布时，直接订到临界分位数。
en: When the demand distribution is known, order straight up to the critical fractile.

zh: 每天的需求独立同分布，分布已知。
en: Daily demand is i.i.d. with a known distribution.

zh: 每天的期望利润最大。
en: Maximize the expected daily profit.

zh:
**定理（临界分位）。** 最优订货量 $q^*=F^{-1}\!\Big(\dfrac{r-c}{r-v}\Big)$，$F$ 是需求的分布函数。证明见"固定订货量"：$\pi(q)$ 是凹的，一阶条件就是这个式子。
这个结构在别处反复出现：银行该留多少准备金（Edgeworth 1888）、航班该超售多少座位、做市商该挂多大的量，都是"多了有一种代价、少了有另一种代价"的分位数问题。统计里，分位数回归的"弹球损失"正是它：最小化 $\mathbb{E}\big[c_u(D-q)^++c_o(q-D)^+\big]$ 的 $q$ 就是 $\dfrac{c_u}{c_u+c_o}$ 分位数。
en:
**Theorem (critical fractile).** The optimal order quantity is $q^*=F^{-1}\!\Big(\dfrac{r-c}{r-v}\Big)$, where $F$ is the distribution function of demand. For the proof see "Fixed order quantity": $\pi(q)$ is concave, and the first-order condition is exactly this equation.
The same structure recurs elsewhere: how much a bank should keep in reserves (Edgeworth 1888), how many seats a flight should overbook and how much size a market maker should quote are all quantile problems of the form "too much has one cost, too little has another". In statistics, the "pinball loss" of quantile regression is exactly this: the $q$ that minimizes $\mathbb{E}\big[c_u(D-q)^++c_o(q-D)^+\big]$ is the $\dfrac{c_u}{c_u+c_o}$ quantile.

zh: 分布记错了（比如按正态去订一个右偏的需求）时，分位数跟着错。
en: When the distribution is misspecified (for example, ordering for a right-skewed demand as if it were normal), the quantile is wrong as well.

zh: 它的得分应与"固定订货量"取 $q^*$ 时完全相同。
en: Its score should be exactly the same as that of "Fixed order quantity" at $q^*$.

zh: 不知道分布：每天订到目前为止见过的需求的经验分位数。
en: The distribution is unknown: each day, order the empirical quantile of the demand seen so far.

zh: 第一天订多少
en: First-day order quantity

zh: 每天的需求独立同分布，分布未知；每天收盘后看得到当天的真实需求（即使缺货）。
en: Daily demand is i.i.d. with an unknown distribution; after closing each day you see that day's true demand (even on a stockout).

zh: 每天的期望利润，同时从数据里把分位数学出来。
en: Expected daily profit, while learning the quantile from the data.

zh:
**样本平均逼近。** 用经验分布 $\hat F_t$ 代替 $F$：$q_t=\hat F_t^{-1}\!\Big(\dfrac{r-c}{r-v}\Big)$。经验分位数几乎必然收敛到真实的分位数，所以它渐近最优；要让期望成本（缺货损失加积压损失）与最优值的相对差距以高概率小于 $\varepsilon$，需要的样本数有不依赖分布的上界（Levi, Roundy & Shmoys 2007）。
代价在计算上：要记住全部历史，存储随天数线性增长；用有序数组时，每天插入一个数是 $O(t)$，取分位数是 $O(1)$。
en:
**Sample average approximation.** Replace $F$ by the empirical distribution $\hat F_t$: $q_t=\hat F_t^{-1}\!\Big(\dfrac{r-c}{r-v}\Big)$. The empirical quantile converges almost surely to the true quantile, so the rule is asymptotically optimal; the number of samples needed for the relative gap between the expected cost (stockout loss plus overstock loss) and the optimum to be below $\varepsilon$ with high probability has an upper bound that does not depend on the distribution (Levi, Roundy & Shmoys 2007).
The price is computational: the whole history has to be remembered, so memory grows linearly with the number of days; with a sorted array, inserting one number a day costs $O(t)$ and reading off the quantile costs $O(1)$.

zh: 头几天样本太少，分位数很不稳。如果缺货时看不到真实的需求（只知道卖光了），数据是被截断的，这个估计会系统性偏低。
en: In the first few days the sample is too small and the quantile is very unstable. If true demand cannot be seen on a stockout (you only know that you sold out), the data are censored and this estimate is systematically too low.

zh: 它的得分应介于"订历史平均数"和"临界分位"之间；天数越多，越接近后者。
en: Its score should lie between those of "Order the historical mean" and "Critical fractile"; the more days, the closer it gets to the latter.

zh: 昨天需求比订货多，今天就多订一点；少了就少订一点。
en: If yesterday's demand exceeded the order, order a little more today; if it fell short, order a little less.

zh: 每天朝昨天的需求挪多远 θ
en: Daily step toward yesterday's demand θ

zh: "昨天卖断货了，今天多进一点。"
en: "We sold out yesterday, so stock a little more today."

zh: 没有显式目标：对最近一次的结果做反应。
en: There is no explicit objective: it reacts to the most recent outcome.

zh:
不是最优。需求独立同分布时，昨天的需求不含关于今天的任何信息，追着它走只是给订货量加了噪声；而且它的长期平均订货量停在需求的均值附近，而不是临界分位数。
**实验（Schweitzer & Cachon 2000）。** 受试者的订货量系统性地偏向需求的均值（"向中间靠"）：需求 $U(1,300)$、售价 12，高利润（进价 3，最优 225）时平均只订 177，低利润（进价 9，最优 75）时平均订到 134。"追着上期走"是论文提出的解释之一。
en:
Not optimal. When demand is i.i.d., yesterday's demand carries no information about today's, so chasing it only adds noise to the order quantity; moreover, its long-run average order quantity sits near the mean of demand, not at the critical fractile.
**Experiment (Schweitzer & Cachon 2000).** Subjects' order quantities are systematically biased toward the mean of demand ("pull to center"): with demand $U(1,300)$ and selling price 12, in the high-margin case (unit cost 3, optimum 225) they ordered only 177 on average, and in the low-margin case (unit cost 9, optimum 75) as much as 134 on average. "Chase last period" is one of the explanations the paper proposes.

zh: 需求真的有惯性（今天高、明天也高）时它反而有道理；独立同分布时纯属添乱。
en: When demand really is persistent (high today, high again tomorrow) it does make sense; when demand is i.i.d. it does nothing but add noise.

zh: 对 $\theta$ 做扫描：$\theta=0$（不追）最好，越追越差。
en: Sweep $\theta$: $\theta=0$ (no chasing) is best, and the harder it chases the worse it does.

zh: 每一回合都出 0。这套玩法的基准。
en: Bid 0 every round. The benchmark for this game.

zh: 没有任何关于公司价值的信息；公司对卖方值 $V\sim U(0,100)$，到你手里值 $mV$，$m<2$。
en: There is no information at all about the company's value; the company is worth $V\sim U(0,100)$ to the seller and $mV$ in your hands, with $m<2$.

zh: 每次收购的期望盈亏。
en: Expected profit and loss (P&L) per acquisition.

zh: **在 $m<2$、没有信息时是最优的。** 出价 $b\in(0,100]$ 的期望盈亏是 $(m/2-1)\,b^2/100<0$（推导见"固定出价"），所以任何正的出价都亏，最优是不出价。
en: **Optimal when $m<2$ and there is no information.** The expected P&L of a bid $b\in(0,100]$ is $(m/2-1)\,b^2/100<0$ (for the derivation see "Fixed bid"), so every positive bid loses money and the optimum is not to bid.

zh: $m>2$ 时应该出 100；有尽调信号时，对足够高的信号应该出价。
en: When $m>2$ you should bid 100; when there is a due-diligence signal, you should bid if the signal is high enough.

zh: 得分恒为 0。
en: The score is always 0.

zh: 每一回合都出同一个价 b。
en: Bid the same amount b every round.

zh: 出价 b
en: Bid b

zh: "它平均值 50，到我手里值 75，出个 60 吧"
en: "It is worth 50 on average, so 75 in my hands; let me bid 60"

zh: 公司对卖方值 $V\sim U(0,100)$，只有卖方知道；到你手里值 $mV$；卖方在 $b\ge V$ 时才卖。
en: The company is worth $V\sim U(0,100)$ to the seller, and only the seller knows this value; in your hands it is worth $mV$; the seller sells only when $b\ge V$.

zh:
**定理（Samuelson & Bazerman 1985 的"收购一家公司"）。** 出价 $0\le b\le100$ 的期望盈亏是
$$\mathbb{E}\,\pi(b)=\int_0^b(mv-b)\,\frac{dv}{100}=\Big(\frac m2-1\Big)\frac{b^2}{100}.$$
$m<2$ 时它对一切 $b>0$ 都是负的，最优出价是 0；$m>2$ 时最优是 100。

**关键的一步。** 对方肯卖，本身就是信息：成交意味着 $V\le b$，这时 $V$ 在 $[0,b]$ 上均匀分布，平均只有 $b/2$，到你手里值 $mb/2$。$m=1.5$ 时是 $0.75\,b<b$：只要成交，平均就亏掉出价的四分之一。天真的算法用的是无条件的平均值 50（"值 75，出 60 有赚"），忘了以"成交"为条件。

**实验（见 Thaler 1988 的综述）。** 九成以上的受试者给出正的出价，多数落在 50 到 75 之间。让 69 名 MBA 学生连做 20 轮、每轮都告知盈亏，只有 5 人学会了出价不超过 1。石油公司竞拍海上油田（Capen, Clapp & Campbell 1971）是同一个现象的现实版本：赢得竞拍的，往往是估价最离谱的那一家。
en:
**Theorem (the "Acquiring a Company" problem of Samuelson & Bazerman 1985).** The expected P&L of a bid $0\le b\le100$ is
$$\mathbb{E}\,\pi(b)=\int_0^b(mv-b)\,\frac{dv}{100}=\Big(\frac m2-1\Big)\frac{b^2}{100}.$$
When $m<2$ it is negative for every $b>0$, and the optimal bid is 0; when $m>2$ the optimum is 100.

**The key step.** The other side's willingness to sell is itself information: a deal means $V\le b$, in which case $V$ is uniformly distributed on $[0,b]$ with a mean of only $b/2$, worth $mb/2$ in your hands. At $m=1.5$ that is $0.75\,b<b$: whenever there is a deal, you lose a quarter of your bid on average. The naive calculation uses the unconditional mean of 50 ("worth 75, so a bid of 60 makes money") and forgets to condition on a "deal".

**Experiments (see the survey by Thaler 1988).** More than nine in ten subjects make a positive bid, most of them between 50 and 75. When 69 MBA students played 20 rounds in a row and were told their P&L after every round, only 5 learned to bid no more than 1. Oil companies bidding for offshore fields (Capen, Clapp & Campbell 1971) are the real-world version of the same phenomenon: the winner of the auction is often the company whose estimate was furthest off.

zh: 有信号时，固定出价浪费了信息。
en: When there is a signal, a fixed bid wastes the information.

zh: 对 $b$ 做扫描：得分与图上的抛物线 $(m/2-1)b^2/100$ 重合，$b=60$ 时每次平均亏 9。把 $m$ 调到 2.5，抛物线开口朝上，最优出价变成 100。
en: Sweep $b$: the score coincides with the parabola $(m/2-1)b^2/100$ on the chart; at $b=60$ the average loss is 9 per acquisition. Set $m$ to 2.5: the parabola opens upward and the optimal bid becomes 100.

zh: 有尽调信号时，出价 = k × 信号。k 小于 1 是打折，大于 1 是加价。
en: With a due-diligence signal, bid = k × signal. k below 1 is a discount, k above 1 a markup.

zh: 倍数 k
en: Multiple k

zh: 默认的 0.8 是"打个八折留点余地"的直觉。对它做扫描，看最好的 k 在 1 的哪一边
en: The default 0.8 is the intuition "take a fifth off to leave some room"; sweep it and see on which side of 1 the best k lies

zh: 出价前看得到一个带噪声的估值 $S=V+\varepsilon$。
en: Before bidding you see a noisy estimate $S=V+\varepsilon$ of the value.

zh:
不是最优，而且"估值有噪声，所以打个折"的直觉在这里方向是反的。出价低于 $V$ 就买不到；而买到的每一家都多值 $(m-1)V$。所以信号够准时，最好的出价在估值**之上**：多出一截来保证成交。信号太低、或者噪声太大时，则干脆不该出价。

$m=1.5$ 时量出来的数：噪声的标准差是 5 时，最好的 $k$ 约 $1.1$（每次赚 16.5，贝叶斯出价是 16.7）；噪声 15 时约 $1.15$（8.6 对 8.9），默认的 $k=0.8$ 只赚 2.0，"信号是多少就出多少"是 7.1；噪声到 40，最好的 $k$ 才降到 $0.8$ 上下，而且那时多数信号下根本不该出价（1.0 对 2.2）。

"成交"这个条件确实会把估高了的情形筛出来，这是赢家诅咒的那一半；另一半是不成交就什么都赚不到。两头怎么权衡，要连同成交的概率一起算，见"贝叶斯出价"。
en:
Not optimal; moreover, the intuition "the estimate is noisy, so shade the bid" points the wrong way here. A bid below $V$ buys nothing, while every company you do buy is worth an extra $(m-1)V$. So when the signal is accurate enough, the best bid is **above** the estimate: you bid a bit extra to make sure the deal goes through. When the signal is too low, or the noise too large, you should not bid at all.

Measured numbers at $m=1.5$: when the standard deviation of the noise is 5, the best $k$ is about $1.1$ (earning 16.5 per acquisition; the Bayesian bid earns 16.7); with noise 15 it is about $1.15$ (8.6 versus 8.9), while the default $k=0.8$ earns only 2.0 and "Bid the signal" earns 7.1; only when the noise reaches 40 does the best $k$ fall to around $0.8$, and by then you should not bid at all for most signals (1.0 versus 2.2).

The condition "deal" does select the cases in which the estimate was too high: that is the winner's-curse half of the story. The other half is that without a deal you earn nothing. How to weigh the two has to be worked out together with the probability of a deal; see "Bayesian bid".

zh: 噪声大时，低估值的公司根本不该出价（任何正的出价都亏），按固定的倍数出价却仍然在出。最好的 $k$ 随噪声的大小变，没有一个到处适用的值。
en: When the noise is large, you should not bid at all for companies with a low estimate (any positive bid loses money), yet bidding by a fixed multiple still bids. The best $k$ changes with the size of the noise; no single value works everywhere.

zh: 在"有估值"的设定下对 $k$ 做扫描：噪声 5 和 15 时峰在 $k\approx1.1$–$1.15$（在估值之上），噪声 40 时峰在 $0.8$ 附近。不管噪声多大，它都不超过"贝叶斯出价"。
en: In a "With an estimate" setting, sweep $k$: with noise 5 and 15 the peak is at $k\approx1.1$–$1.15$ (above the estimate); with noise 40 the peak is near $0.8$. However large the noise, it never does better than "Bayesian bid".

zh: 把"对方肯卖"当作信息：对每一个可能的信号，算出条件期望盈亏最大的出价。
en: Treat "the other side is willing to sell" as information: for every possible signal, compute the bid with the highest conditional expected P&L.

zh: $V\sim U(0,100)$，信号 $S=V+\varepsilon$，$\varepsilon\sim N(0,\sigma_s^2)$ 与 $V$ 独立，这些你都知道。
en: The value is $V\sim U(0,100)$, the signal is $S=V+\varepsilon$, and the noise $\varepsilon\sim N(0,\sigma_s^2)$ is independent of $V$; you know all of this.

zh: 给定信号 $s$ 时的条件期望盈亏 $\displaystyle\int_0^b(mv-b)\,f(v\mid s)\,dv$。
en: The conditional expected profit and loss (P&L) given the signal $s$: $\displaystyle\int_0^b(mv-b)\,f(v\mid s)\,dv$.

zh:
**逐点最优。** 后验密度 $f(v\mid s)\propto\mathbf 1_{[0,100]}(v)\,\varphi\!\big((s-v)/\sigma_s\big)$。对每个 $s$ 取使上面的积分最大的 $b$；若最大值不为正，就不出价。内点解满足一阶条件
$$(m-1)\,b\,f(b\mid s)=F(b\mid s).$$
左边是把出价抬高一点多买到的那批"刚好值 $b$"的公司带来的利润，右边是为原本就能成交的公司多付的钱。代码里把 $v$ 和 $s$ 离散化，对每个信号扫一遍出价，计算量 $O(N_s\cdot N_v)$，结果存成一张表。
噪声相对于价值水平很大时，低信号下任何出价都是亏的：比如 $\sigma_s=15$、$s=30$ 时最优是不出价。信号越准，敢出价的范围越大，利润越接近没有信息不对称时的 $(m-1)\,\mathbb{E}V=25$。
en:
**Pointwise optimal.** The posterior density is $f(v\mid s)\propto\mathbf 1_{[0,100]}(v)\,\varphi\!\big((s-v)/\sigma_s\big)$. For each $s$, take the $b$ that maximizes the integral above; if the maximum is not positive, do not bid. An interior solution satisfies the first-order condition
$$(m-1)\,b\,f(b\mid s)=F(b\mid s).$$
The left side is the profit from the additional companies "worth exactly $b$" that are bought when the bid is raised slightly; the right side is the extra money paid for the companies that would have been bought anyway. The code discretizes $v$ and $s$ and scans the bids once for each signal, at a cost of $O(N_s\cdot N_v)$, and stores the result as a table.
When the noise is large relative to the level of the value, every bid loses money at low signals: for example, at $\sigma_s=15$ and $s=30$ the optimum is not to bid. The more accurate the signal, the wider the range of signals at which it is willing to bid, and the closer the profit comes to the $(m-1)\,\mathbb{E}V=25$ obtained when there is no information asymmetry.

zh: 噪声的大小、先验的范围记错时，表就不对。
en: When the size of the noise or the range of the prior is misspecified, the table is wrong.

zh: 在"有估值"的设定下，它应胜过"按估值的倍数出价"里任何一个固定的 $k$。把噪声从 5 调到 40：利润从约 17 降到约 2，规则下方显示的出价表里，越来越多的信号对应"不出价"。
en: In a "With an estimate" setting, it should beat "Bid a multiple of the estimate" at any fixed $k$. Raise the noise from 5 to 40: the profit falls from about 17 to about 2, and in the bid table shown below the rule more and more signals correspond to "no bid".

zh: 把 11 档出价当成 11 台老虎机，用 ε-贪心去试。
en: Treat 11 bid levels as 11 bandit arms and try them out with ε-greedy.

zh: 没试过的档位的初始估计
en: Initial estimate for untried levels

zh: 不知道盈亏的公式，只看得到每次出价之后的盈亏。
en: The formula for the P&L is unknown; you see only the P&L after each bid.

zh: 每次收购的平均盈亏，边试边学。
en: Average profit and loss (P&L) per acquisition, learning by trial and error.

zh:
不是最优：它不理解问题的结构，只是把每一档出价的平均盈亏记下来。$m<2$ 时所有正的出价平均都亏，它最终会学到"出 0"，但一直保留的 $\varepsilon$ 试探让它持续小亏。
它说明了为什么真人在这个问题上学得慢：高出价的盈亏波动很大（成交了可能大赚，也可能大亏），要很多次才能看出平均是负的；而低出价很少成交，几乎没有反馈。
en:
Not optimal: it does not understand the structure of the problem and merely records the average P&L of each bid level. When $m<2$ every positive bid loses on average, and it eventually learns to "bid 0", but the $\varepsilon$ exploration that it never gives up keeps it losing a little.
It shows why real people learn slowly in this problem: the P&L of high bids is very volatile (a deal may win big or lose big), so it takes many rounds to see that the average is negative; low bids rarely lead to a deal and give almost no feedback.

zh: 回合数少时来不及学；有信号时它完全没有用到信号。
en: With few rounds there is not enough time to learn; when there is a signal, it makes no use of it at all.

zh: $m=1.5$ 时得分略低于 0（试探的代价）；$m=2.5$ 时它能学到出高价。
en: At $m=1.5$ the score is slightly below 0 (the cost of exploration); at $m=2.5$ it learns to bid high.

zh: 每天都持有净值的 f 倍。
en: Hold a position of f times account equity every day.

zh: 仓位（杠杆倍数）f
en: Position (leverage multiple) f

zh: 价格是几何布朗运动，漂移 $\mu$、波动 $\sigma$；净值到 $1+a$ 即通过，到 $1-b$ 即出局。
en: The price is a geometric Brownian motion with drift $\mu$ and volatility $\sigma$; you pass as soon as account equity reaches $1+a$ and are knocked out as soon as it reaches $1-b$.

zh: 通过率：在期限内、出局之前碰到目标的概率。
en: Pass rate: the probability of hitting the target within the deadline and before being knocked out.

zh:
**定理一（没有优势时的上限）。** 若价格是鞅（$\mu=0$）且没有交易成本，则不论用什么规则，净值 $W_t$ 都是鞅。设 $\tau$ 是考核结束的时刻，由可选停时定理 $\mathbb{E}W_\tau=1$；通过时 $W_\tau=1+a$，其余情形 $W_\tau\ge1-b$，所以
$$\mathbb{P}(\text{通过})\le\frac{b}{a+b}.$$
目标和亏损线都是 10% 时，上限是 $\tfrac12$；杠杆很高时一天之内见分晓，起作用的是单日亏损线 $d$，通过率趋于 $\dfrac{d}{a+d}$（$d=5\%$ 时是 $\tfrac13$）。建仓本身的成本也要从 $d$ 里扣：成本 2 个基点时，10 倍杠杆先付掉净值的 0.2%，50 倍付掉 1%（通过率约 0.27），100 倍付掉 2%（约 0.20）。

**定理二（固定杠杆、不设期限）。** 连续调仓使仓位恒为 $f$ 时，$W$ 是几何布朗运动，$W^{-\theta}$ 是鞅，$\theta=\dfrac{2\mu}{f\sigma^2}-1$。于是
$$\mathbb{P}(\text{先到 }1+a)=\frac{1-(1-b)^{-\theta}}{(1+a)^{-\theta}-(1-b)^{-\theta}}.$$
$\theta>0$ 当且仅当 $f<2\mu/\sigma^2$（Kelly 比例的两倍）；恰好相等时 $\theta=0$，上式取极限，是 $\dfrac{-\ln(1-b)}{\ln(1+a)-\ln(1-b)}$。$\mu>0$ 时杠杆越低这个概率越高，$f\to0$ 时趋于 1，但所需的时间趋于无穷。**期限**逼着你加杠杆，**单日亏损线**又不许你加太多，通过率因此在中间有一个峰。
en:
**Theorem 1 (the upper bound when there is no edge).** If the price is a martingale ($\mu=0$) and there are no trading costs, then whatever rule is used, account equity $W_t$ is a martingale. Let $\tau$ be the time at which the challenge ends; by the optional stopping theorem $\mathbb{E}W_\tau=1$; on a pass $W_\tau=1+a$, and in every other case $W_\tau\ge1-b$, so
$$\mathbb{P}(\text{pass})\le\frac{b}{a+b}.$$
When the target and the loss line are both 10%, the upper bound is $\tfrac12$; at very high leverage the outcome is settled within a single day, the line that matters is the daily loss limit $d$, and the pass rate tends to $\dfrac{d}{a+d}$ ($\tfrac13$ when $d=5\%$). The cost of opening the position itself also has to come out of $d$: at a cost of 2 basis points, 10× leverage pays 0.2% of account equity up front, 50× pays 1% (pass rate about 0.27) and 100× pays 2% (about 0.20).

**Theorem 2 (fixed leverage, no deadline).** When continuous rebalancing keeps the position constant at $f$, $W$ is a geometric Brownian motion and $W^{-\theta}$ is a martingale, where $\theta=\dfrac{2\mu}{f\sigma^2}-1$. Hence
$$\mathbb{P}(\text{first reaches }1+a)=\frac{1-(1-b)^{-\theta}}{(1+a)^{-\theta}-(1-b)^{-\theta}}.$$
Here $\theta>0$ if and only if $f<2\mu/\sigma^2$ (twice the Kelly fraction); at equality $\theta=0$ and the expression above is taken as a limit, which is $\dfrac{-\ln(1-b)}{\ln(1+a)-\ln(1-b)}$. When $\mu>0$, the lower the leverage the higher this probability, and it tends to 1 as $f\to0$, but the time required tends to infinity. The **deadline** forces you to add leverage, while the **daily loss limit** does not let you add too much, so the pass rate has a peak in between.

zh: 通过率最高的杠杆几乎不取决于你的优势，只取决于目标、期限和波动（大致要让 $f\sigma\sqrt{\text{期限}}$ 与目标同一量级）：默认设定下，漂移 $\mu$ 从 0 到 40%，峰都在 1.75 倍上下。它和使长期增长率最高的杠杆（Kelly 比例 $\mu/\sigma^2$）没有关系：优势很小时远高于 Kelly（$\mu=2\%$ 时 Kelly 只有 0.5 倍），默认的 $\mu=10\%$ 时 Kelly 是 2.5 倍，反而比它高。考核奖励的是"在限期内冲过一条线"，不是长期经营，这正是这类考核被批评的地方。
en: The leverage with the highest pass rate hardly depends on your edge; it depends only on the target, the deadline and the volatility (roughly, $f\sigma\sqrt{\text{deadline}}$ should be of the same order of magnitude as the target): under the default settings, as the drift $\mu$ goes from 0 to 40%, the peak stays around 1.75×. It has nothing to do with the leverage that maximizes the long-run growth rate (the Kelly fraction $\mu/\sigma^2$): when the edge is small it is far above Kelly (at $\mu=2\%$ Kelly is only 0.5×), whereas at the default $\mu=10\%$ Kelly is 2.5× and is the higher of the two. The challenge rewards "getting across a line before the deadline", not trading for the long run, and that is exactly what this kind of challenge is criticized for.

zh: 对 $f$ 做扫描：通过率先升后降再趋平，图上的理论曲线（不设期限）在低杠杆处远高于模拟，差的就是期限。把 $\mu$ 设为 0：任何杠杆下通过率都不超过上面的上限。
en: Sweep $f$: the pass rate rises, then falls, then levels off; the theoretical curve on the chart (no deadline) lies far above the simulation at low leverage, and the difference is the deadline. Set $\mu$ to 0: at any leverage the pass rate does not exceed the upper bound above.

zh: 离出局线近了就缩，快到目标了也收一收。
en: Shrink the position when close to the knockout line; ease off when close to the target as well.

zh: 平时的仓位 f
en: Normal position f

zh: 离目标多近开始收
en: Distance to the target at which to start easing off

zh: 快达标时至少保留的仓位
en: Minimum position kept near the target

zh: "别死在线上，也别在终点前摔倒。"
en: "Don't die at the line, and don't stumble just before the finish."

zh: 通过率，同时让"碰线出局"的结局少一些。
en: Pass rate, while making "knocked out at a line" endings less frequent.

zh:
没有最优性保证。离出局线近时按比例减仓，类似固定比例组合保险（CPPI）：连续交易时净值永远碰不到底线，代价是越接近底线越难翻身，最后多半死于"到期没达标"。没有优势时，定理一的上限对它同样成立：调仓方式改变的只是失败的方式，不是通过率的上限。
期限到期、目标为期末净值越过某条线的问题有精确解（Browne 1999）：最优策略等价于复制一张数字期权，离期限越近、离目标越远，仓位越大。
en:
No optimality guarantee. Reducing the position in proportion when close to the knockout line resembles constant-proportion portfolio insurance (CPPI): with continuous trading, account equity never touches the floor; the price is that the closer it gets to the floor the harder it is to recover, and in the end it mostly dies of "Deadline reached, target missed". With no edge, the upper bound of Theorem 1 holds for it as well: the way you rebalance changes only how you fail, not the upper bound on the pass rate.
The problem with a fixed deadline, in which the goal is for account equity at the deadline to be above a given line, has an exact solution (Browne 1999): the optimal strategy is equivalent to replicating a digital option, and the closer the deadline and the farther the target, the larger the position.

zh: 减仓之后翻身更慢，更容易超时。
en: After the position is reduced, recovery is slower and running out of time is more likely.

zh: 默认的缓冲（0.05）在按天调仓时几乎不起作用：成绩和同样仓位的固定仓位分不出来。把"离出局线多近开始减仓"调到 0.1 以上再看失败的构成："碰到总亏损线出局"的比例降到接近 0，"到期没达标"的比例升上来（0.1 时约 7%，0.2 时约 44%），通过率基本不变。
en: The default buffer (0.05) has almost no effect with daily rebalancing: its results cannot be told apart from those of a fixed position of the same size. Raise "Distance to the knockout line at which to start cutting" to 0.1 or above and look at the breakdown of failures: the share of "Knocked out at the total-loss line" falls to nearly 0 and the share of "Deadline reached, target missed" rises (about 7% at 0.1, about 44% at 0.2), while the pass rate is essentially unchanged.

zh: 把仓位定在一个 k 倍标准差的坏日子也碰不到单日亏损线的水平。
en: Set the position at a level where even a bad day of k standard deviations would not hit the daily loss limit.

zh: 估计波动用的天数
en: Days used to estimate volatility

zh: 要扛得住几个标准差 k
en: Number of standard deviations to withstand k

zh: 数据不够时的仓位
en: Position when data are insufficient

zh: 日收益大致对称，波动可以用最近几天的数据估计。
en: Daily returns are roughly symmetric, and volatility can be estimated from the last few days of data.

zh: 让"单日亏损超限"几乎不发生。
en: Make "knocked out by the daily loss limit" almost never happen.

zh: 没有最优性保证。它只管住了一种失败方式：仓位 $f$ 下一天亏掉 $d$ 需要价格跌 $d/f$，令它等于 $k$ 个标准差，得 $f=d/(k\hat\sigma)$。$k$ 大了仓位太小，在期限内到不了目标；$k$ 小了单日亏损线照碰。厚尾的行情里，"$k$ 个标准差"对应的概率比正态时大得多。
en: No optimality guarantee. It guards against only one way of failing: at position $f$, losing $d$ in one day requires the price to fall by $d/f$; setting that equal to $k$ standard deviations gives $f=d/(k\hat\sigma)$. If $k$ is large the position is too small to reach the target within the deadline; if $k$ is small the daily loss limit gets hit all the same. In a heavy-tailed market, the probability that corresponds to "$k$ standard deviations" is much larger than under the normal distribution.

zh: 期限短时它太慢；波动估计滞后时，暴涨暴跌的第一天挡不住。
en: With a short deadline it is too slow; when the volatility estimate lags, it cannot stop the first day of a violent move up or down.

zh: 对 $k$ 做扫描：通过率单峰。把行情换成厚尾：同样的 $k$，单日亏损超限的比例上升。
en: Sweep $k$: the pass rate is single-peaked. Switch the market to heavy tails: for the same $k$, the share knocked out by the daily loss limit rises.

zh: 第一个时段满仓买入，一直拿到最后。这套玩法的基准。
en: Go fully invested in the first slot and hold to the end. The benchmark for this game.

zh: 不是最优，但它几乎不受这套制度影响：只买一次、不卖，T+1 和印花税都碰不到它；涨跌停只是把大消息的兑现推迟几天，不改变它最终拿到的收益。所以它是衡量"制度让主动交易多付了多少"的参照物。
